lessons.title: Try This (Section 1.2(a))
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Factorization splits the middle term into two parts whose product equals the product of the first and last coefficients and whose sum is the middle coefficient.
  • For a² + 7a - 8 = 0 the middle term 7a is split as 8a - a, giving (a + 8)(a - 1) = 0.
  • The zero-product property says if a product of factors is zero, at least one factor is zero.
  • a² + 7a - 8 = 0 has solution set {-8, 1}.
  • For 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0 the middle term 7p is split as 15p - 8p, since 15 × (-8) = -120 = 6 × (-20).
  • 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0 factorises as (2p + 5)(3p - 4) = 0, with solution set {-5/2, 4/3}.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the following equation: a² + 7a - 8 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
a² + 7a - 8 = 0
Split the middle term 7a into 8a - a, because 8 × (-1) = -8 and 8 + (-1) = 7:
a² + 8a - a - 8 = 0
a(a + 8) - 1(a + 8) = 0
(a + 8)(a - 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
a + 8 = 0 or a - 1 = 0
a = -8 or a = 1
Check: for a = 1: 1 + 7 - 8 = 0 (true); for a = -8: 64 - 56 - 8 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-8, 1}

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the following equation: 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
6p² + 7p - 20 = 0
Split the middle term 7p into 15p - 8p, because 15 × (-8) = -120 = 6 × (-20) and 15 + (-8) = 7:
6p² + 15p - 8p - 20 = 0
3p(2p + 5) - 4(2p + 5) = 0
(2p + 5)(3p - 4) = 0
By the zero-product property:
2p + 5 = 0 or 3p - 4 = 0
p = -(5)/(2) or p = (4)/(3)
Check: for p = (4)/(3): 6 × (16)/(9) + 7 × (4)/(3) - 20 = (32)/(3) + (28)/(3) - 20 = 20 - 20 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-(5)/(2), (4)/(3)}

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: a² + 7a - 8 = 0. What is the solution set?
In solving a² + 7a - 8 = 0 by factorization, the middle term 7a is split as
mcqs.why: We need two numbers with product 1 × (-8) = -8 and sum 7. The numbers 8 and -1 satisfy 8 × (-1) = -8 and 8 + (-1) = 7, so 7a is split as 8a - a.

mcqs.q: The factorised form of a² + 7a - 8 is
mcqs.why: Grouping after splitting the middle term: a² + 8a - a - 8 = a(a + 8) - 1(a + 8) = (a + 8)(a - 1), which expands back to a² + 7a - 8.

mcqs.q: Which property is used after writing (a + 8)(a - 1) = 0 to find the roots?
mcqs.why: The zero-product property states that if a product of two factors equals zero, then at least one factor is zero, so a + 8 = 0 or a - 1 = 0, giving a = -8 or a = 1.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0. What is the solution set?
In solving 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0, the middle term 7p is split as
mcqs.why: We need two numbers with product 6 × (-20) = -120 and sum 7. The numbers 15 and -8 satisfy 15 × (-8) = -120 and 15 + (-8) = 7, so 7p is split as 15p - 8p.

mcqs.q: The factorised form of 6p² + 7p - 20 is
mcqs.why: Grouping: 6p² + 15p - 8p - 20 = 3p(2p + 5) - 4(2p + 5) = (2p + 5)(3p - 4), and expanding (2p + 5)(3p - 4) gives 6p² + 7p - 20.

mcqs.q: From the factor 2p + 5 = 0 in 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0, the value of p is
mcqs.why: Solving the linear factor step by step: 2p + 5 = 0, subtract 5 from both sides to get 2p = -5, then divide both sides by 2 to get p = -5/2.

mcqs.q: Why are 15 and -8 chosen when splitting the middle term of 6p² + 7p - 20 = 0?
options: Because both are factors of 20 only
mcqs.why: The split numbers must multiply to a × c = 6 × (-20) = -120 and add to b = 7. Check: 15 × (-8) = -120 and 15 + (-8) = 7, so both conditions hold.

mcqs.q: Which value checks correctly in a² + 7a - 8 = 0?
mcqs.why: Substitute a = 1 into the left side step by step: (1)² + 7(1) - 8 = 1 + 7 - 8 = 0, so a = 1 satisfies the equation and is one of its roots.

lessons.title: Try This (Section 1.2(b))
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To complete the square, add the square of half the coefficient of the variable.
  • For y² + 3y, half of 3 is 3/2 and (3/2)² = 9/4 must be added.
  • y² + 3y + 9/4 = (y + 3/2)² is a perfect square.
  • For q² - 4q, half of -4 is -2 and (-2)² = 4 must be added.
  • q² - 4q + 4 = (q - 2)² is a perfect square.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). What must be added to obtain a perfect square? y² + 3y

Ans: By completing the square:
The coefficient of y is 3.
Half of the coefficient of y is (3)/(2).
Square half the coefficient of y: ((3)/(2))² = (9)/(4).
So (9)/(4) must be added.
y² + 3y + (9)/(4) = (y + (3)/(2))², which is a perfect square.
Answer: (9)/(4)

Q: Q1(ii). What must be added to obtain a perfect square? q² - 4q

Ans: By completing the square:
The coefficient of q is -4.
Half of the coefficient of q is -2.
Square half the coefficient of q: (-2)² = 4.
So 4 must be added.
q² - 4q + 4 = (q - 2)², which is a perfect square.
Answer: 4

mcqs.q: What must be added to y² + 3y to obtain a perfect square?
mcqs.why: The coefficient of y is 3. Half of the coefficient is 3/2, and squaring it gives (3/2)² = 9/4, so 9/4 must be added to make a perfect square.

mcqs.q: What must be added to q² - 4q to obtain a perfect square?
mcqs.why: The coefficient of q is -4. Half of the coefficient is -2, and squaring it gives (-2)² = 4, so 4 must be added to make a perfect square.

mcqs.q: y² + 3y + 9/4 written as a perfect square is
mcqs.why: Adding (3/2)² = 9/4 completes the square: y² + 3y + 9/4 = (y + 3/2)², and expanding (y + 3/2)² gives y² + 3y + 9/4 back again.

mcqs.q: q² - 4q + 4 written as a perfect square is
mcqs.why: Adding (-2)² = 4 completes the square: q² - 4q + 4 = (q - 2)², and expanding (q - 2)² gives q² - 4q + 4 back again.

mcqs.q: Half of the coefficient of y in y² + 3y is
mcqs.why: The coefficient of y is 3, and half of it is found by dividing by 2: 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2. This half is then squared in the completing-the-square method.

mcqs.q: Half of the coefficient of q in q² - 4q is
mcqs.why: The coefficient of q is -4, and half of it is found by dividing by 2: -4 ÷ 2 = -2. Squaring this half, (-2)² = 4, gives the number to add.

mcqs.q: The value of (3/2)² is
mcqs.why: Squaring a fraction squares the numerator and the denominator separately: (3/2)² = 3²/2² = 9/4. This is the quantity added to y² + 3y.

mcqs.q: The value of (-2)² is
mcqs.why: A negative number squared becomes positive: (-2)² = (-2) × (-2) = 4. This is the quantity added to q² - 4q to complete the square.

mcqs.q: In the completing-the-square method, the number added is
options: The coefficient of the variable itself
The square of half the coefficient of the variable
The square of the coefficient of the variable
mcqs.why: As used in both items: take the coefficient of the variable, halve it, then square the result — for y² + 3y this gives (3/2)² = 9/4 and for q² - 4q it gives (-2)² = 4.

mcqs.q: The coefficient of q in the expression q² - 4q is
mcqs.why: The term containing q to the first power is -4q, so its coefficient, including the sign, is -4. Half of -4 is -2, whose square is the 4 that must be added.

lessons.title: Try This (Section 1.3)
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The quadratic formula is x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a).
  • For 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0, a = 4, b = 3, c = -2 and the discriminant is 9 + 32 = 41.
  • 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0 has solution set {(-3 + √41)/8, (-3 - √41)/8}.
  • For 9x² - 42x + 49 = 0 the discriminant is 1764 - 1764 = 0, so the roots are equal.
  • 9x² - 42x + 49 = (3x - 7)², with the single root x = 7/3.
  • For 5x² - 10x + 13 = 0 the discriminant is 100 - 260 = -160, negative, so there is no real solution.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve: 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 4, b = 3 and c = -2.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-3 ± √(3² - 4(4)(-2)))/(2(4))
x = (-3 ± √(9 + 32))/(8)
x = (-3 ± √41)/(8)
Solution set: {(-3 + √41)/(8), (-3 - √41)/(8)}

Q: Q1(ii). Solve: 9x² - 42x + 49 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 9, b = -42 and c = 49.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-42) ± √((-42)² - 4(9)(49)))/(2(9))
x = (42 ± √(1764 - 1764))/(18)
x = (42 ± √0)/(18)
x = (42)/(18) = (7)/(3)
The discriminant is zero, so the two roots are equal (indeed 9x² - 42x + 49 = (3x - 7)²).
Solution set: {(7)/(3)}

Q: Q1(iii). Solve: 5x² - 10x + 13 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 5, b = -10 and c = 13.
First find the discriminant b² - 4ac:
b² - 4ac = (-10)² - 4(5)(13)
b² - 4ac = 100 - 260 = -160
The discriminant is negative, so √(b² - 4ac) = √(-160) is not a real number.
Answer: the equation has no real solution.
Note: as printed, the discriminant of this equation is negative, so it has no real roots.

mcqs.q: Using the quadratic formula for 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0, the values of a, b and c are
mcqs.why: Comparing 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0 term by term: the x² coefficient gives a = 4, the x coefficient gives b = 3, and the constant gives c = -2.

mcqs.q: The discriminant of 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0 is
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 4, b = 3, c = -2: substitute to get 3² - 4(4)(-2) = 9 + 32 = 41, so the discriminant is 41.

mcqs.q: The solution set of 4x² + 3x - 2 = 0 is
The discriminant of 9x² - 42x + 49 = 0 is
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 9, b = -42, c = 49: substitute to get (-42)² - 4(9)(49) = 1764 - 1764 = 0, so the discriminant is zero.

mcqs.q: Because the discriminant of 9x² - 42x + 49 = 0 is zero, its roots are
mcqs.why: A zero discriminant makes the ± part of the formula vanish: x = 42/18 = 7/3 only. Indeed 9x² - 42x + 49 = (3x - 7)², confirming equal roots.

mcqs.q: The solution set of 9x² - 42x + 49 = 0 is
mcqs.why: Formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). Substitute a = 9, b = -42, c = 49: x = (42 ± √0) / 18 = 42/18 = 7/3, a single repeated root.

mcqs.q: 9x² - 42x + 49 expressed as a perfect square is
mcqs.why: Expand (3x - 7)² step by step: (3x)² - 2(3x)(7) + 7² = 9x² - 42x + 49, which matches the given expression exactly, so it is a perfect square.

mcqs.q: The discriminant of 5x² - 10x + 13 = 0 is
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 5, b = -10, c = 13: substitute to get (-10)² - 4(5)(13) = 100 - 260 = -160, so the discriminant is -160.

mcqs.q: Since the discriminant of 5x² - 10x + 13 = 0 is negative, the equation has
mcqs.why: The formula needs √(-160), and the square root of a negative number is not a real number, so 5x² - 10x + 13 = 0 has no real solution.

mcqs.q: In the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a), the expression under the square root is called
mcqs.why: The expression b² - 4ac is the discriminant. Its sign decides the nature of the roots: positive gives real unequal roots, zero gives equal roots, and negative gives no real roots.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • x² + 5x + 4 = 0 factorises as (x + 4)(x + 1) = 0, with solution set {-4, -1}.
  • x² + 3x - 10 = 0 factorises as (x + 5)(x - 2) = 0, with solution set {-5, 2}.
  • Completing the square on x² + 6x - 40 = 0 gives (x + 3)² = 49 and roots 4 and -10.
  • Completing the square on x² - 10x + 11 = 0 gives (x - 5)² = 14 and roots 5 ± √14.
  • By the quadratic formula, x² - 8x + 15 = 0 has roots 3 and 5, and 6x² - 17x + 12 = 0 has roots 3/2 and 4/3.
  • If (y + 13)(y + a) has no linear term then 13 + a = 0, so a = -13.
  • For y² - 7y - 9 = 0, α + β = 7 and αβ = -9, so the positive difference of the roots is √(49 + 36) = √85.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the following equation by factorization: x² + 5x + 4 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
x² + 5x + 4 = 0
Split the middle term 5x into 4x + x, because 4 × 1 = 4 and 4 + 1 = 5:
x² + 4x + x + 4 = 0
x(x + 4) + 1(x + 4) = 0
(x + 4)(x + 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x + 4 = 0 or x + 1 = 0
x = -4 or x = -1
Check: for x = -1: 1 - 5 + 4 = 0 (true); for x = -4: 16 - 20 + 4 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-1, -4}

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the following equation by factorization: (x - 3)² = 4

Ans: By factorization:
(x - 3)² = 4
Expand the left-hand side:
x² - 6x + 9 = 4
x² - 6x + 5 = 0
Split the middle term -6x into -5x - x:
x² - 5x - x + 5 = 0
x(x - 5) - 1(x - 5) = 0
(x - 5)(x - 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x - 5 = 0 or x - 1 = 0
x = 5 or x = 1
Check: for x = 5: (5 - 3)² = 4 (true); for x = 1: (1 - 3)² = 4 (true)
Solution set: {1, 5}

Q: Q1(iii). Solve the following equation by factorization: x² + 3x - 10 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
x² + 3x - 10 = 0
Split the middle term 3x into 5x - 2x, because 5 × (-2) = -10 and 5 + (-2) = 3:
x² + 5x - 2x - 10 = 0
x(x + 5) - 2(x + 5) = 0
(x + 5)(x - 2) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x + 5 = 0 or x - 2 = 0
x = -5 or x = 2
Check: for x = 2: 4 + 6 - 10 = 0 (true); for x = -5: 25 - 15 - 10 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-5, 2}

Q: Q1(iv). Solve the following equation by factorization: 6x² - 13x + 5 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
6x² - 13x + 5 = 0
Split the middle term -13x into -10x - 3x, because (-10) × (-3) = 30 = 6 × 5 and -10 + (-3) = -13:
6x² - 10x - 3x + 5 = 0
2x(3x - 5) - 1(3x - 5) = 0
(3x - 5)(2x - 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
3x - 5 = 0 or 2x - 1 = 0
x = (5)/(3) or x = (1)/(2)
Check: for x = (1)/(2): 6 × (1)/(4) - 13 × (1)/(2) + 5 = (3)/(2) - (13)/(2) + 5 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {(1)/(2), (5)/(3)}

Q: Q1(v). Solve the following equation by factorization: 3(x² - 1) = 4(x + 1)

Ans: By factorization:
3(x² - 1) = 4(x + 1)
Expand both sides:
3x² - 3 = 4x + 4
Bring all terms to the left-hand side:
3x² - 4x - 7 = 0
Split the middle term -4x into -7x + 3x:
3x² - 7x + 3x - 7 = 0
x(3x - 7) + 1(3x - 7) = 0
(3x - 7)(x + 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
3x - 7 = 0 or x + 1 = 0
x = (7)/(3) or x = -1
Check: for x = -1: 3(1 - 1) = 0 and 4(-1 + 1) = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-1, (7)/(3)}

Q: Q1(vi). Solve the following equation by factorization: x(3x - 5) = (x - 6)(x - 7)

Ans: By factorization:
x(3x - 5) = (x - 6)(x - 7)
Expand both sides:
3x² - 5x = x² - 13x + 42
Bring all terms to the left-hand side:
2x² + 8x - 42 = 0
Divide both sides by 2:
x² + 4x - 21 = 0
Split the middle term 4x into 7x - 3x:
x² + 7x - 3x - 21 = 0
x(x + 7) - 3(x + 7) = 0
(x + 7)(x - 3) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x + 7 = 0 or x - 3 = 0
x = -7 or x = 3
Check: for x = 3: 3(9 - 5) = 12 and (3 - 6)(3 - 7) = 12 (true)
Solution set: {3, -7}

Q: Q2(i). Solve the following equation by completing the square: x² + 6x - 40 = 0

Ans: By completing the square:
x² + 6x - 40 = 0
Shift the constant term to the right-hand side:
x² + 6x = 40
Half of the coefficient of x is 3, and 3² = 9; add 9 to both sides:
x² + 6x + 9 = 40 + 9
(x + 3)² = 49
Take the square root of both sides:
x + 3 = ±7
x = -3 + 7 or x = -3 - 7
x = 4 or x = -10
Check: for x = 4: 16 + 24 - 40 = 0 (true); for x = -10: 100 - 60 - 40 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-10, 4}

Q: Q2(ii). Solve the following equation by completing the square: x² - 10x + 11 = 0

Ans: By completing the square:
x² - 10x + 11 = 0
Shift the constant term to the right-hand side:
x² - 10x = -11
Half of the coefficient of x is -5, and (-5)² = 25; add 25 to both sides:
x² - 10x + 25 = -11 + 25
(x - 5)² = 14
Take the square root of both sides:
x - 5 = ±√14
x = 5 ± √14
Solution set: {5 + √14, 5 - √14}

Q: Q2(iii). Solve the following equation by completing the square: 4x² + 12x = 0

Ans: By completing the square:
4x² + 12x = 0
Divide both sides by 4 so that the coefficient of x² is 1:
x² + 3x = 0
Half of the coefficient of x is (3)/(2), and ((3)/(2))² = (9)/(4); add (9)/(4) to both sides:
x² + 3x + (9)/(4) = (9)/(4)
(x + (3)/(2))² = (9)/(4)
Take the square root of both sides:
x + (3)/(2) = ±(3)/(2)
x = -(3)/(2) + (3)/(2) or x = -(3)/(2) - (3)/(2)
x = 0 or x = -3
Check: for x = -3: 4(9) + 12(-3) = 36 - 36 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {0, -3}

Q: Q2(iv). Solve the following equation by completing the square: 5x² - 10x - 840 = 0

Ans: By completing the square:
5x² - 10x - 840 = 0
Divide both sides by 5 so that the coefficient of x² is 1:
x² - 2x - 168 = 0
Shift the constant term to the right-hand side:
x² - 2x = 168
Half of the coefficient of x is -1, and (-1)² = 1; add 1 to both sides:
x² - 2x + 1 = 168 + 1
(x - 1)² = 169
Take the square root of both sides:
x - 1 = ±13
x = 1 + 13 or x = 1 - 13
x = 14 or x = -12
Check: for x = 14: 5(196) - 140 - 840 = 980 - 980 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-12, 14}

Q: Q2(v). Solve the following equation by completing the square: 9x² - 6x + (5)/(9) = 0

Ans: By completing the square:
9x² - 6x + (5)/(9) = 0
Divide both sides by 9 so that the coefficient of x² is 1:
x² - (2)/(3)x + (5)/(81) = 0
Shift the constant term to the right-hand side:
x² - (2)/(3)x = -(5)/(81)
Half of the coefficient of x is -(1)/(3), and (-(1)/(3))² = (1)/(9) = (9)/(81); add (1)/(9) to both sides:
x² - (2)/(3)x + (1)/(9) = -(5)/(81) + (9)/(81)
(x - (1)/(3))² = (4)/(81)
Take the square root of both sides:
x - (1)/(3) = ±(2)/(9)
x = (1)/(3) + (2)/(9) or x = (1)/(3) - (2)/(9)
x = (5)/(9) or x = (1)/(9)
Check: for x = (1)/(9): 9 × (1)/(81) - 6 × (1)/(9) + (5)/(9) = (1)/(9) - (6)/(9) + (5)/(9) = 0 (true)
Solution set: {(1)/(9), (5)/(9)}

Q: Q2(vi). Solve the following equation by completing the square: (x - 1)(x + 3) = 5(x + 2) - 3

Ans: By completing the square:
(x - 1)(x + 3) = 5(x + 2) - 3
Expand both sides:
x² + 2x - 3 = 5x + 7
Bring all terms to the left-hand side:
x² - 3x - 10 = 0
Shift the constant term to the right-hand side:
x² - 3x = 10
Half of the coefficient of x is -(3)/(2), and (-(3)/(2))² = (9)/(4); add (9)/(4) to both sides:
x² - 3x + (9)/(4) = 10 + (9)/(4)
(x - (3)/(2))² = (49)/(4)
Take the square root of both sides:
x - (3)/(2) = ±(7)/(2)
x = (3)/(2) + (7)/(2) or x = (3)/(2) - (7)/(2)
x = 5 or x = -2
Check: for x = 5: (4)(8) = 32 and 5(7) - 3 = 32 (true); for x = -2: (-3)(1) = -3 and 5(0) - 3 = -3 (true)
Solution set: {-2, 5}

Q: Q3(i). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: x² - 8x + 15 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 1, b = -8 and c = 15.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-8) ± √((-8)² - 4(1)(15)))/(2(1))
x = (8 ± √(64 - 60))/(2)
x = (8 ± √4)/(2)
x = (8 ± 2)/(2)
x = (10)/(2) or x = (6)/(2)
x = 5 or x = 3
Solution set: {3, 5}

Q: Q3(ii). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: x² - 2x - 4 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 1, b = -2 and c = -4.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-2) ± √((-2)² - 4(1)(-4)))/(2(1))
x = (2 ± √(4 + 16))/(2)
x = (2 ± √20)/(2)
x = (2 ± 2√5)/(2)
x = 1 ± √5
Solution set: {1 + √5, 1 - √5}

Q: Q3(iii). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: 4x² + 3x = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Write the equation in standard form: 4x² + 3x + 0 = 0.
Here a = 4, b = 3 and c = 0.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-3 ± √(3² - 4(4)(0)))/(2(4))
x = (-3 ± √9)/(8)
x = (-3 ± 3)/(8)
x = (0)/(8) or x = (-6)/(8)
x = 0 or x = -(3)/(4)
Solution set: {0, -(3)/(4)}

Q: Q3(iv). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: 3x(x - 2) + 1 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Expand and write in standard form:
3x² - 6x + 1 = 0
Here a = 3, b = -6 and c = 1.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-6) ± √((-6)² - 4(3)(1)))/(2(3))
x = (6 ± √(36 - 12))/(6)
x = (6 ± √24)/(6)
x = (6 ± 2√6)/(6)
x = 1 ± (√6)/(3)
Solution set: {1 + (√6)/(3), 1 - (√6)/(3)}

Q: Q3(v). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: 6x² - 17x + 12 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 6, b = -17 and c = 12.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-17) ± √((-17)² - 4(6)(12)))/(2(6))
x = (17 ± √(289 - 288))/(12)
x = (17 ± √1)/(12)
x = (17 ± 1)/(12)
x = (18)/(12) or x = (16)/(12)
x = (3)/(2) or x = (4)/(3)
Solution set: {(3)/(2), (4)/(3)}

Q: Q3(vi). Solve the following equation by quadratic formula: (x²)/(3) - (x)/(12) = (1)/(24)

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Multiply both sides by 24 to clear the fractions:
8x² - 2x = 1
Write in standard form:
8x² - 2x - 1 = 0
Here a = 8, b = -2 and c = -1.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
x = (-(-2) ± √((-2)² - 4(8)(-1)))/(2(8))
x = (2 ± √(4 + 32))/(16)
x = (2 ± √36)/(16)
x = (2 ± 6)/(16)
x = (8)/(16) or x = (-4)/(16)
x = (1)/(2) or x = -(1)/(4)
Solution set: {(1)/(2), -(1)/(4)}

Q: Q4(i). Find all solutions to the following equation: t² - 8t + 7 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
t² - 8t + 7 = 0
Split the middle term -8t into -7t - t:
t² - 7t - t + 7 = 0
t(t - 7) - 1(t - 7) = 0
(t - 7)(t - 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
t - 7 = 0 or t - 1 = 0
t = 7 or t = 1
Solution set: {1, 7}

Q: Q4(ii). Find all solutions to the following equation: 72 + 6x = x²

Ans: By factorization:
72 + 6x = x²
Bring all terms to one side:
x² - 6x - 72 = 0
Split the middle term -6x into -12x + 6x:
x² - 12x + 6x - 72 = 0
x(x - 12) + 6(x - 12) = 0
(x - 12)(x + 6) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x - 12 = 0 or x + 6 = 0
x = 12 or x = -6
Check: for x = 12: 72 + 72 = 144 = 12² (true); for x = -6: 72 - 36 = 36 = (-6)² (true)
Solution set: {12, -6}

Q: Q4(iii). Find all solutions to the following equation: r² + 4r + 1 = 0

Ans: Using the quadratic formula: r = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 1, b = 4 and c = 1.
Substitute the values of a, b and c:
r = (-4 ± √(4² - 4(1)(1)))/(2(1))
r = (-4 ± √(16 - 4))/(2)
r = (-4 ± √12)/(2)
r = (-4 ± 2√3)/(2)
r = -2 ± √3
Solution set: {-2 + √3, -2 - √3}

Q: Q4(iv). Find all solutions to the following equation: x(x + 10) = 10(-10 - x)

Ans: By factorization:
x(x + 10) = 10(-10 - x)
Expand both sides:
x² + 10x = -100 - 10x
Bring all terms to the left-hand side:
x² + 20x + 100 = 0
The left-hand side is a perfect square:
(x + 10)² = 0
Take the square root of both sides:
x + 10 = 0
x = -10
Check: for x = -10: -10(0) = 0 and 10(-10 + 10) = 0 (true)
Solution set: {-10}

Q: Q5. The equation (y + 13)(y + a) has no linear term. Find value of a.

Ans: Expand the product:
(y + 13)(y + a) = y² + ay + 13y + 13a
(y + 13)(y + a) = y² + (13 + a)y + 13a
The linear term is (13 + a)y.
The equation has no linear term, so the coefficient of y must be zero:
13 + a = 0
a = -13
Answer: a = -13

Q: Q6. The equation ax² + 5x = 3 has x = 1 as a solution. What is the other solution?

Ans: Since x = 1 is a solution, substitute x = 1 in the equation:
a(1)² + 5(1) = 3
a + 5 = 3
a = -2
So the equation becomes:
-2x² + 5x = 3
-2x² + 5x - 3 = 0
Multiply both sides by -1:
2x² - 5x + 3 = 0
By factorization, split -5x into -3x - 2x:
2x² - 3x - 2x + 3 = 0
x(2x - 3) - 1(2x - 3) = 0
(2x - 3)(x - 1) = 0
By the zero-product property:
2x - 3 = 0 or x - 1 = 0
x = (3)/(2) or x = 1
Answer: the other solution is (3)/(2)

Q: Q7. What is the positive difference of the roots of y² - 7y - 9 = 0?

Ans: Let the roots be α and β.
For y² - 7y - 9 = 0, comparing with ay² + by + c = 0 gives a = 1, b = -7, c = -9.
Sum of the roots: α + β = -(b)/(a) = 7
Product of the roots: αβ = (c)/(a) = -9
Use the identity (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ:
(α - β)² = (7)² - 4(-9)
(α - β)² = 49 + 36 = 85
Take the positive square root:
α - β = √85
Answer: the positive difference of the roots is √85

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: x² + 5x + 4 = 0.
mcqs.why: Split 5x as 4x + x since 4 × 1 = 4 and 4 + 1 = 5: x(x + 4) + 1(x + 4) = (x + 4)(x + 1) = 0, so x + 4 = 0 or x + 1 = 0, giving x = -4 or x = -1.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: (x - 3)² = 4.
mcqs.why: Expand: x² - 6x + 9 = 4, so x² - 6x + 5 = 0. Split -6x as -5x - x: (x - 5)(x - 1) = 0, so x - 5 = 0 or x - 1 = 0, giving x = 5 or x = 1.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: x² + 3x - 10 = 0.
Solve by factorization: 6x² - 13x + 5 = 0.
After expanding and rearranging, 3(x² - 1) = 4(x + 1) becomes
mcqs.why: Expand both sides: 3x² - 3 = 4x + 4. Bring everything to the left: 3x² - 3 - 4x - 4 = 3x² - 4x - 7 = 0, which then factorises as (3x - 7)(x + 1) = 0.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x² + 6x - 40 = 0.
mcqs.why: Move the constant: x² + 6x = 40. Half of 6 is 3 and 3² = 9, so add 9 to both sides: (x + 3)² = 49, hence x + 3 = ±7, giving x = 4 or x = -10.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x² - 10x + 11 = 0.
mcqs.why: Move the constant: x² - 10x = -11. Half of -10 is -5 and (-5)² = 25, so add 25 to both sides: (x - 5)² = 14, hence x - 5 = ±√14 and x = 5 ± √14.

mcqs.q: In completing the square for 5x² - 10x - 840 = 0, the first step is to divide by 5, giving
mcqs.why: Divide every term by 5 so the x² coefficient becomes 1: 5x²/5 = x², -10x/5 = -2x and -840/5 = -168, giving x² - 2x - 168 = 0, whose roots are 14 and -12.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: 9x² - 6x + 5/9 = 0.
mcqs.why: Divide by 9: x² - (2/3)x = -5/81. Half of -2/3 is -1/3 and its square is 1/9, so (x - 1/3)² = 4/81, hence x - 1/3 = ±2/9, giving x = 5/9 or x = 1/9.

mcqs.q: Solve by the quadratic formula: x² - 8x + 15 = 0.
Solve by the quadratic formula: x² - 2x - 4 = 0.
Solve by the quadratic formula: 6x² - 17x + 12 = 0.
Find all solutions of x(x + 10) = 10(-10 - x).
mcqs.why: Expand: x² + 10x = -100 - 10x, so x² + 20x + 100 = 0. The left side is the perfect square (x + 10)² = 0, so x + 10 = 0 and the only solution is x = -10.

mcqs.q: The equation (y + 13)(y + a) has no linear term. The value of a is
mcqs.why: Expand: (y + 13)(y + a) = y² + (13 + a)y + 13a. No linear term means its coefficient is zero: 13 + a = 0, so a = -13.

mcqs.q: The positive difference of the roots of y² - 7y - 9 = 0 is
mcqs.why: Here α + β = -b/a = 7 and αβ = c/a = -9. Use (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ = 7² - 4(-9) = 49 + 36 = 85, and taking the positive square root gives α - β = √85.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Equations in x⁴ and x² are solved by the substitution y = x², turning them into quadratics.
  • x⁴ - 5x² + 4 = 0 gives y = 4 or y = 1, hence x = ±2 or x = ±1.
  • For x + 1/x substitutions, (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2, so x² + 1/x² = y² - 2.
  • For x - 1/x substitutions, x² + 1/x² = t² + 2 where t = x - 1/x.
  • Exponential equations are solved by substituting y = 3ˣ or y = 5ˣ and using equal bases.
  • Products of four linear factors are paired so both pairs share the same x² + kx part, then substituted.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the following equation: x⁴ - 5x² + 4 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = x², so x⁴ = y².
The equation becomes:
y² - 5y + 4 = 0
By factorization, split -5y into -4y - y:
y² - 4y - y + 4 = 0
y(y - 4) - 1(y - 4) = 0
(y - 4)(y - 1) = 0
y = 4 or y = 1
Substitute back y = x²:
x² = 4 or x² = 1
x = ±2 or x = ±1
Solution set: {±1, ±2}

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the following equation: x⁴ - 7x² + 12 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = x², so x⁴ = y².
The equation becomes:
y² - 7y + 12 = 0
By factorization, split -7y into -4y - 3y:
y² - 4y - 3y + 12 = 0
y(y - 4) - 3(y - 4) = 0
(y - 4)(y - 3) = 0
y = 4 or y = 3
Substitute back y = x²:
x² = 4 or x² = 3
x = ±2 or x = ±√3
Solution set: {±2, ±√3}

Q: Q1(iii). Solve the following equation: 6x⁴ - 13x² + 5 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = x², so x⁴ = y².
The equation becomes:
6y² - 13y + 5 = 0
By factorization, split -13y into -10y - 3y:
6y² - 10y - 3y + 5 = 0
2y(3y - 5) - 1(3y - 5) = 0
(3y - 5)(2y - 1) = 0
y = (5)/(3) or y = (1)/(2)
Substitute back y = x²:
x² = (5)/(3) or x² = (1)/(2)
x = ±√((5)/(3)) or x = ±(1)/(√2)
Solution set: {±√((5)/(3)), ±(1)/(√2)}

Q: Q1(iv). Solve the following equation: x + 2 - (1)/(x + 2) = (3)/(2)

Ans: By substitution:
Let u = x + 2.
The equation becomes:
u - (1)/(u) = (3)/(2)
Multiply both sides by 2u:
2u² - 2 = 3u
2u² - 3u - 2 = 0
By factorization, split -3u into -4u + u:
2u² - 4u + u - 2 = 0
2u(u - 2) + 1(u - 2) = 0
(u - 2)(2u + 1) = 0
u = 2 or u = -(1)/(2)
Substitute back u = x + 2:
x + 2 = 2 gives x = 0
x + 2 = -(1)/(2) gives x = -(5)/(2)
Solution set: {0, -(5)/(2)}

Q: Q1(v). Solve the following equation: x - (4)/(x) = 2

Ans: Multiply both sides by x (x ≠ 0):
x² - 4 = 2x
x² - 2x - 4 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 1, b = -2 and c = -4.
x = (-(-2) ± √((-2)² - 4(1)(-4)))/(2(1))
x = (2 ± √(4 + 16))/(2)
x = (2 ± √20)/(2)
x = (2 ± 2√5)/(2)
x = 1 ± √5
Solution set: {1 + √5, 1 - √5}

Q: Q1(vi). Solve the following equation: (x + 2)/(x - 2) - (x - 2)/(x + 2) = (5)/(6)

Ans: Take the LCM (x - 2)(x + 2) = x² - 4 on the left-hand side:
((x + 2)² - (x - 2)²)/(x² - 4) = (5)/(6)
Expand the squares in the numerator:
(x² + 4x + 4) - (x² - 4x + 4) = 8x
So the equation becomes:
(8x)/(x² - 4) = (5)/(6)
Cross-multiply:
48x = 5(x² - 4)
48x = 5x² - 20
5x² - 48x - 20 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
Here a = 5, b = -48 and c = -20.
x = (48 ± √((-48)² - 4(5)(-20)))/(2(5))
x = (48 ± √(2304 + 400))/(10)
x = (48 ± √2704)/(10)
x = (48 ± 52)/(10)
x = (100)/(10) or x = (-4)/(10)
x = 10 or x = -(2)/(5)
Solution set: {10, -(2)/(5)}

Q: Q1(vii). Solve the following equation: 3(x² + (1)/(x²)) - 16(x + (1)/(x)) + 26 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = x + (1)/(x).
Squaring both sides: y² = x² + (1)/(x²) + 2, so x² + (1)/(x²) = y² - 2.
Substitute in the given equation:
3(y² - 2) - 16y + 26 = 0
3y² - 6 - 16y + 26 = 0
3y² - 16y + 20 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: y = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
y = (16 ± √((-16)² - 4(3)(20)))/(2(3))
y = (16 ± √(256 - 240))/(6)
y = (16 ± 4)/(6)
y = (10)/(3) or y = 2
Case 1: y = 2, that is x + (1)/(x) = 2.
Multiply by x: x² + 1 = 2x
x² - 2x + 1 = 0
(x - 1)² = 0, so x = 1
Case 2: y = (10)/(3), that is x + (1)/(x) = (10)/(3).
Multiply by 3x: 3x² + 3 = 10x
3x² - 10x + 3 = 0
By factorization, split -10x into -9x - x:
3x² - 9x - x + 3 = 0
3x(x - 3) - 1(x - 3) = 0
(x - 3)(3x - 1) = 0
x = 3 or x = (1)/(3)
Solution set: {1, 3, (1)/(3)}

Q: Q1(viii). Solve the following equation: (x + (1)/(x))² - 10(x + (1)/(x)) + 16 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = x + (1)/(x).
The equation becomes:
y² - 10y + 16 = 0
By factorization, split -10y into -8y - 2y:
y² - 8y - 2y + 16 = 0
y(y - 8) - 2(y - 8) = 0
(y - 8)(y - 2) = 0
y = 8 or y = 2
Case 1: y = 2, that is x + (1)/(x) = 2.
Multiply by x: x² + 1 = 2x
x² - 2x + 1 = 0
(x - 1)² = 0, so x = 1
Case 2: y = 8, that is x + (1)/(x) = 8.
Multiply by x: x² + 1 = 8x
x² - 8x + 1 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (8 ± √(64 - 4))/(2)
x = (8 ± √60)/(2)
x = (8 ± 2√15)/(2)
x = 4 ± √15
Solution set: {1, 4 + √15, 4 - √15}

Q: Q1(ix). Solve the following equation: (x² + (1)/(x²)) - (x - (1)/(x)) - 4 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let t = x - (1)/(x).
Squaring both sides: t² = x² + (1)/(x²) - 2, so x² + (1)/(x²) = t² + 2.
Substitute in the given equation:
(t² + 2) - t - 4 = 0
t² - t - 2 = 0
By factorization, split -t into -2t + t:
t² - 2t + t - 2 = 0
t(t - 2) + 1(t - 2) = 0
(t - 2)(t + 1) = 0
t = 2 or t = -1
Case 1: t = 2, that is x - (1)/(x) = 2.
Multiply by x: x² - 1 = 2x
x² - 2x - 1 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (2 ± √(4 + 4))/(2) = (2 ± 2√2)/(2) = 1 ± √2
Case 2: t = -1, that is x - (1)/(x) = -1.
Multiply by x: x² - 1 = -x
x² + x - 1 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-1 ± √(1 + 4))/(2) = (-1 ± √5)/(2)
Solution set: {1 + √2, 1 - √2, (-1 + √5)/(2), (-1 - √5)/(2)}

Q: Q1(x). Solve the following equation: 3²ˣ - 10.3ˣ + 9 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Write 3²ˣ = (3ˣ)².
Let y = 3ˣ.
The equation becomes:
y² - 10y + 9 = 0
By factorization, split -10y into -9y - y:
y² - 9y - y + 9 = 0
y(y - 9) - 1(y - 9) = 0
(y - 9)(y - 1) = 0
y = 9 or y = 1
Substitute back y = 3ˣ:
3ˣ = 9 = 3² gives x = 2
3ˣ = 1 = 3⁰ gives x = 0
Solution set: {2, 0}

Q: Q1(xi). Solve the following equation: 3.3²ˣ⁺¹ - 10.3ˣ + 1 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Write 3²ˣ⁺¹ = 3.(3ˣ)², so 3.3²ˣ⁺¹ = 9(3ˣ)².
Let y = 3ˣ.
The equation becomes:
9y² - 10y + 1 = 0
By factorization, split -10y into -9y - y:
9y² - 9y - y + 1 = 0
9y(y - 1) - 1(y - 1) = 0
(y - 1)(9y - 1) = 0
y = 1 or y = (1)/(9)
Substitute back y = 3ˣ:
3ˣ = 1 = 3⁰ gives x = 0
3ˣ = (1)/(9) = 3⁻² gives x = -2
Solution set: {0, -2}

Q: Q1(xii). Solve the following equation: 5ˣ⁺¹ + 5²⁻ˣ = 126

Ans: By substitution:
Write 5ˣ⁺¹ = 5.5ˣ and 5²⁻ˣ = (25)/(5ˣ).
Let y = 5ˣ.
The equation becomes:
5y + (25)/(y) = 126
Multiply both sides by y:
5y² + 25 = 126y
5y² - 126y + 25 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: y = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
y = (126 ± √((-126)² - 4(5)(25)))/(2(5))
y = (126 ± √(15876 - 500))/(10)
y = (126 ± √15376)/(10)
y = (126 ± 124)/(10)
y = (250)/(10) or y = (2)/(10)
y = 25 or y = (1)/(5)
Substitute back y = 5ˣ:
5ˣ = 25 = 5² gives x = 2
5ˣ = (1)/(5) = 5⁻¹ gives x = -1
Solution set: {-1, 2}

Q: Q1(xiii). Solve the following equation: (x - 3)(x + 9)(x + 5)(x - 7) = 385

Ans: Pair the factors whose x-coefficients match: (-3) + 5 = 9 + (-7) = 2.
[(x - 3)(x + 5)][(x + 9)(x - 7)] = 385
Expand each pair:
(x - 3)(x + 5) = x² + 2x - 15
(x + 9)(x - 7) = x² + 2x - 63
So (x² + 2x - 15)(x² + 2x - 63) = 385.
By substitution, let u = x² + 2x:
(u - 15)(u - 63) = 385
u² - 78u + 945 = 385
u² - 78u + 560 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: u = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
u = (78 ± √(6084 - 2240))/(2)
u = (78 ± √3844)/(2)
u = (78 ± 62)/(2)
u = 70 or u = 8
Case 1: u = 70, that is x² + 2x = 70.
x² + 2x - 70 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-2 ± √(4 + 280))/(2) = (-2 ± √284)/(2) = (-2 ± 2√71)/(2) = -1 ± √71
Case 2: u = 8, that is x² + 2x = 8.
x² + 2x - 8 = 0
By factorization: (x + 4)(x - 2) = 0, so x = -4 or x = 2
Solution set: {-1 + √71, -1 - √71, 2, -4}

Q: Q1(xiv). Solve the following equation: (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) + 1 = 0

Ans: Pair the factors whose x-coefficients match: 1 + 4 = 2 + 3 = 5.
[(x + 1)(x + 4)][(x + 2)(x + 3)] + 1 = 0
Expand each pair:
(x + 1)(x + 4) = x² + 5x + 4
(x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 5x + 6
By substitution, let u = x² + 5x:
(u + 4)(u + 6) + 1 = 0
u² + 10u + 24 + 1 = 0
u² + 10u + 25 = 0
(u + 5)² = 0
u = -5
Substitute back u = x² + 5x:
x² + 5x = -5
x² + 5x + 5 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (-5 ± √(25 - 20))/(2)
x = (-5 ± √5)/(2)
Solution set: {(-5 + √5)/(2), (-5 - √5)/(2)}

Q: Q1(xv). Solve the following equation: (x + 1)(x + 3)(x + 5)(x + 7) + 16 = 0

Ans: Pair the factors whose x-coefficients match: 1 + 7 = 3 + 5 = 8.
[(x + 1)(x + 7)][(x + 3)(x + 5)] + 16 = 0
Expand each pair:
(x + 1)(x + 7) = x² + 8x + 7
(x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 8x + 15
By substitution, let u = x² + 8x:
(u + 7)(u + 15) + 16 = 0
u² + 22u + 105 + 16 = 0
u² + 22u + 121 = 0
(u + 11)² = 0
u = -11
Substitute back u = x² + 8x:
x² + 8x = -11
x² + 8x + 11 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (-8 ± √(64 - 44))/(2)
x = (-8 ± √20)/(2)
x = (-8 ± 2√5)/(2)
x = -4 ± √5
Solution set: {-4 + √5, -4 - √5}

Q: Q2. Solve the equation x⁴ - 2x³ - 2x² + 2x + 1 = 0

Ans: x = 0 is not a solution (it gives 1 = 0), so divide both sides by x²:
x² - 2x - 2 + (2)/(x) + (1)/(x²) = 0
Group the terms:
(x² + (1)/(x²)) - 2(x - (1)/(x)) - 2 = 0
By substitution, let t = x - (1)/(x).
Squaring both sides: t² = x² + (1)/(x²) - 2, so x² + (1)/(x²) = t² + 2.
Substitute in the equation:
(t² + 2) - 2t - 2 = 0
t² - 2t = 0
t(t - 2) = 0
t = 0 or t = 2
Case 1: t = 0, that is x - (1)/(x) = 0.
Multiply by x: x² - 1 = 0, so x = ±1
Case 2: t = 2, that is x - (1)/(x) = 2.
Multiply by x: x² - 2x - 1 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (2 ± √(4 + 4))/(2) = (2 ± 2√2)/(2) = 1 ± √2
Solution set: {±1, 1 + √2, 1 - √2}

mcqs.q: Solve: x⁴ - 5x² + 4 = 0.
mcqs.why: Let y = x²: y² - 5y + 4 = (y - 4)(y - 1) = 0, so y = 4 or y = 1. Substituting back, x² = 4 gives x = ±2 and x² = 1 gives x = ±1.

mcqs.q: Solve: x⁴ - 7x² + 12 = 0.
mcqs.why: Let y = x²: y² - 7y + 12 = (y - 4)(y - 3) = 0, so y = 4 or y = 3. Substituting back, x² = 4 gives x = ±2 and x² = 3 gives x = ±√3.

mcqs.q: In solving x - 4/x = 2, after multiplying both sides by x the equation becomes
mcqs.why: Multiply each term by x: x · x = x², x · (-4/x) = -4 and x · 2 = 2x, giving x² - 4 = 2x, i.e. x² - 2x - 4 = 0, whose roots by the formula are 1 ± √5.
Let u = x + 2: u - 1/u = 3/2, multiply by 2u to get 2u² - 3u - 2 = (u - 2)(2u + 1) = 0, so u = 2 or u = -1/2. Then x + 2 = 2 gives x = 0 and x + 2 = -1/2 gives x = -5/2.
With LCM x² - 4 the numerator is (x + 2)² - (x - 2)² = 8x, so 8x/(x² - 4) = 5/6 and 5x² - 48x - 20 = 0. Formula: x = (48 ± √(2304 + 400)) / 10 = (48 ± 52) / 10, giving x = 10 or x = -2/5.

mcqs.q: If y = x + 1/x, then x² + 1/x² equals
mcqs.why: Square y: y² = (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2(x)(1/x) + 1/x² = x² + 1/x² + 2. Rearranging this identity gives x² + 1/x² = y² - 2.

mcqs.q: In solving (x + 1/x)² - 10(x + 1/x) + 16 = 0, the substitution y = x + 1/x gives y =
mcqs.why: The equation becomes y² - 10y + 16 = 0. Split -10y as -8y - 2y: (y - 8)(y - 2) = 0, so y = 8 or y = 2, leading to x = 1 and x = 4 ± √15.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3²ˣ - 10·3ˣ + 9 = 0.
mcqs.why: Write 3²ˣ = (3ˣ)² and let y = 3ˣ: y² - 10y + 9 = (y - 9)(y - 1) = 0, so y = 9 or y = 1. Then 3ˣ = 9 = 3² gives x = 2 and 3ˣ = 1 = 3⁰ gives x = 0.

mcqs.q: Solve: 5ˣ⁺¹ + 5²⁻ˣ = 126.
mcqs.why: Let y = 5ˣ: 5y + 25/y = 126, multiply by y to get 5y² - 126y + 25 = 0. Formula: y = (126 ± √(15876 - 500)) / 10 = (126 ± 124) / 10, so y = 25 or y = 1/5, giving x = 2 or x = -1.

mcqs.q: To solve x⁴ - 2x³ - 2x² + 2x + 1 = 0, after dividing by x² the substitution used is
mcqs.why: Dividing by x² and grouping gives (x² + 1/x²) - 2(x - 1/x) - 2 = 0. With t = x - 1/x we have x² + 1/x² = t² + 2, leading to t² - 2t = 0 and finally x = ±1, 1 ± √2.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Radical equations are solved by isolating a radical and squaring both sides.
  • Squaring can introduce extraneous roots, so every candidate must be checked in the original equation.
  • √(5x + 21) = x + 3 gives candidates -4 and 3, but only 3 checks, so the solution set is {3}.
  • With two radicals, square, isolate the remaining radical, then square again.
  • Substitution u = x² + 2x simplifies √(x² + 2x + 4) + √(x² + 2x + 9) = 5 to √(u + 4) + √(u + 9) = 5.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the following equation: √(5x + 21) = x + 3

Ans: Square both sides to remove the radical:
5x + 21 = (x + 3)²
5x + 21 = x² + 6x + 9
Bring all terms to one side:
x² + x - 12 = 0
By factorization, split x into 4x - 3x:
x² + 4x - 3x - 12 = 0
x(x + 4) - 3(x + 4) = 0
(x + 4)(x - 3) = 0
x = -4 or x = 3
Check in the original equation:
For x = 3: √(15 + 21) = √36 = 6 and 3 + 3 = 6 (true)
For x = -4: √(-20 + 21) = √1 = 1 and -4 + 3 = -1 (false), so x = -4 is an extraneous root
Solution set: {3}

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the following equation: √(2x - 1) = x - 2

Ans: Square both sides to remove the radical:
2x - 1 = (x - 2)²
2x - 1 = x² - 4x + 4
Bring all terms to one side:
x² - 6x + 5 = 0
By factorization, split -6x into -5x - x:
x² - 5x - x + 5 = 0
x(x - 5) - 1(x - 5) = 0
(x - 5)(x - 1) = 0
x = 5 or x = 1
Check in the original equation:
For x = 5: √(10 - 1) = √9 = 3 and 5 - 2 = 3 (true)
For x = 1: √(2 - 1) = √1 = 1 and 1 - 2 = -1 (false), so x = 1 is an extraneous root
Solution set: {5}

Q: Q1(iii). Solve the following equation: √(4x + 5) = 2x - 5

Ans: Square both sides to remove the radical:
4x + 5 = (2x - 5)²
4x + 5 = 4x² - 20x + 25
Bring all terms to one side:
4x² - 24x + 20 = 0
Divide both sides by 4:
x² - 6x + 5 = 0
By factorization, split -6x into -5x - x:
x² - 5x - x + 5 = 0
x(x - 5) - 1(x - 5) = 0
(x - 5)(x - 1) = 0
x = 5 or x = 1
Check in the original equation:
For x = 5: √(20 + 5) = √25 = 5 and 2(5) - 5 = 5 (true)
For x = 1: √(4 + 5) = √9 = 3 and 2(1) - 5 = -3 (false), so x = 1 is an extraneous root
Solution set: {5}

Q: Q1(iv). Solve the following equation: √(29 - 4x) = 2x + 3

Ans: Square both sides to remove the radical:
29 - 4x = (2x + 3)²
29 - 4x = 4x² + 12x + 9
Bring all terms to one side:
4x² + 16x - 20 = 0
Divide both sides by 4:
x² + 4x - 5 = 0
By factorization, split 4x into 5x - x:
x² + 5x - x - 5 = 0
x(x + 5) - 1(x + 5) = 0
(x + 5)(x - 1) = 0
x = -5 or x = 1
Check in the original equation:
For x = 1: √(29 - 4) = √25 = 5 and 2(1) + 3 = 5 (true)
For x = -5: √(29 + 20) = √49 = 7 and 2(-5) + 3 = -7 (false), so x = -5 is an extraneous root
Solution set: {1}

Q: Q1(v). Solve the following equation: √(x + 7) + √(x + 2) = √(6x + 13)

Ans: Square both sides:
(x + 7) + (x + 2) + 2√((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 6x + 13
2x + 9 + 2√((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 6x + 13
Isolate the remaining radical:
2√((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 4x + 4
√((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 2x + 2
Square both sides again:
(x + 7)(x + 2) = (2x + 2)²
x² + 9x + 14 = 4x² + 8x + 4
Bring all terms to one side:
3x² - x - 10 = 0
By factorization, split -x into -6x + 5x:
3x² - 6x + 5x - 10 = 0
3x(x - 2) + 5(x - 2) = 0
(x - 2)(3x + 5) = 0
x = 2 or x = -(5)/(3)
Check in the original equation:
For x = 2: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5 and √(12 + 13) = √25 = 5 (true)
For x = -(5)/(3): the step √((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 2x + 2 would need a square root to equal the negative number 2(-(5)/(3)) + 2 = -(4)/(3), so x = -(5)/(3) is an extraneous root
Solution set: {2}

Q: Q1(vi). Solve the following equation: √(x) + √(3x + 1) = √(5x + 1)

Ans: The equation is defined for x ≥ 0.
Square both sides:
x + (3x + 1) + 2√(x(3x + 1)) = 5x + 1
4x + 1 + 2√(3x² + x) = 5x + 1
Isolate the remaining radical:
2√(3x² + x) = x
Square both sides again:
4(3x² + x) = x²
12x² + 4x = x²
11x² + 4x = 0
By factorization:
x(11x + 4) = 0
x = 0 or x = -(4)/(11)
Check in the original equation:
For x = 0: √0 + √1 = 1 and √1 = 1 (true)
x = -(4)/(11) is rejected because the equation is only defined for x ≥ 0 (√(x) is not real for negative x)
Solution set: {0}

Q: Q1(vii). Solve the following equation: √(6x + 40) - √(x + 21) = √(x + 5)

Ans: Isolate one radical:
√(6x + 40) = √(x + 21) + √(x + 5)
Square both sides:
6x + 40 = (x + 21) + (x + 5) + 2√((x + 21)(x + 5))
6x + 40 = 2x + 26 + 2√((x + 21)(x + 5))
Isolate the remaining radical:
4x + 14 = 2√((x + 21)(x + 5))
2x + 7 = √((x + 21)(x + 5))
Square both sides again:
(2x + 7)² = (x + 21)(x + 5)
4x² + 28x + 49 = x² + 26x + 105
Bring all terms to one side:
3x² + 2x - 56 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (-2 ± √(4 + 672))/(6)
x = (-2 ± √676)/(6)
x = (-2 ± 26)/(6)
x = 4 or x = -(14)/(3)
Check in the original equation:
For x = 4: √(24 + 40) - √(4 + 21) = √64 - √25 = 8 - 5 = 3 and √(4 + 5) = √9 = 3 (true)
For x = -(14)/(3): √(6x + 40) - √(x + 21) is negative while √(x + 5) is positive, so x = -(14)/(3) is an extraneous root
Solution set: {4}

Q: Q1(viii). Solve the following equation: √(2x - 3) + √(2x + 4) = √(6x + 13)

Ans: Square both sides:
(2x - 3) + (2x + 4) + 2√((2x - 3)(2x + 4)) = 6x + 13
4x + 1 + 2√((2x - 3)(2x + 4)) = 6x + 13
Isolate the remaining radical:
2√((2x - 3)(2x + 4)) = 2x + 12
√((2x - 3)(2x + 4)) = x + 6
Square both sides again:
(2x - 3)(2x + 4) = (x + 6)²
4x² + 2x - 12 = x² + 12x + 36
Bring all terms to one side:
3x² - 10x - 48 = 0
Using the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (10 ± √(100 + 576))/(6)
x = (10 ± √676)/(6)
x = (10 ± 26)/(6)
x = 6 or x = -(8)/(3)
Check in the original equation:
For x = 6: √(12 - 3) + √(12 + 4) = √9 + √16 = 3 + 4 = 7 and √(36 + 13) = √49 = 7 (true)
x = -(8)/(3) is rejected because 2x - 3 < 0, so √(2x - 3) is not real
Solution set: {6}

Q: Q1(ix). Solve the following equation: √(x² + 2x + 4) + √(x² + 2x + 9) = 5

Ans: By substitution, let u = x² + 2x.
The equation becomes:
√(u + 4) + √(u + 9) = 5
Isolate one radical:
√(u + 9) = 5 - √(u + 4)
Square both sides:
u + 9 = 25 + (u + 4) - 10√(u + 4)
u + 9 = u + 29 - 10√(u + 4)
Isolate the remaining radical:
10√(u + 4) = 20
√(u + 4) = 2
Square both sides:
u + 4 = 4
u = 0
Substitute back u = x² + 2x:
x² + 2x = 0
By factorization:
x(x + 2) = 0
x = 0 or x = -2
Check in the original equation:
For x = 0: √4 + √9 = 2 + 3 = 5 (true)
For x = -2: √(4 - 4 + 4) + √(4 - 4 + 9) = √4 + √9 = 2 + 3 = 5 (true)
Solution set: {0, -2}

Q: Q1(x). Solve the following equation: √(2x² + 3x + 5) + √(2x² + 3x + 1) = 2

Ans: By substitution, let u = 2x² + 3x.
The equation becomes:
√(u + 5) + √(u + 1) = 2
Isolate one radical:
√(u + 5) = 2 - √(u + 1)
Square both sides:
u + 5 = 4 + (u + 1) - 4√(u + 1)
u + 5 = u + 5 - 4√(u + 1)
So 4√(u + 1) = 0, which gives:
u + 1 = 0
u = -1
Substitute back u = 2x² + 3x:
2x² + 3x = -1
2x² + 3x + 1 = 0
By factorization, split 3x into 2x + x:
2x² + 2x + x + 1 = 0
2x(x + 1) + 1(x + 1) = 0
(x + 1)(2x + 1) = 0
x = -1 or x = -(1)/(2)
Check in the original equation:
For x = -1: √(2 - 3 + 5) + √(2 - 3 + 1) = √4 + √0 = 2 + 0 = 2 (true)
For x = -(1)/(2): √((1)/(2) - (3)/(2) + 5) + √((1)/(2) - (3)/(2) + 1) = √4 + √0 = 2 (true)
Solution set: {-(1)/(2), -1}

Q: Q2. Find 2x + 5 if x satisfies √(40 - 9x) - 2√(7 - x) = √(-x)

Ans: Isolate the first radical:
√(40 - 9x) = √(-x) + 2√(7 - x)
Square both sides:
40 - 9x = (-x) + 4(7 - x) + 4√((-x)(7 - x))
40 - 9x = 28 - 5x + 4√(x² - 7x)
Isolate the remaining radical:
12 - 4x = 4√(x² - 7x)
Divide both sides by 4:
3 - x = √(x² - 7x)
Square both sides again:
(3 - x)² = x² - 7x
9 - 6x + x² = x² - 7x
9 - 6x = -7x
9 = -x
x = -9
Check in the original equation:
√(40 - 9(-9)) - 2√(7 - (-9)) = √121 - 2√16 = 11 - 8 = 3 and √(-(-9)) = √9 = 3 (true)
Now find the required value:
2x + 5 = 2(-9) + 5 = -18 + 5 = -13
Answer: 2x + 5 = -13

mcqs.why: Square both sides: 5x + 21 = x² + 6x + 9, so x² + x - 12 = (x + 4)(x - 3) = 0, giving x = -4 or x = 3. Check x = -4: √1 = 1 but -4 + 3 = -1, so it is extraneous; only x = 3 remains.

mcqs.q: In √(5x + 21) = x + 3, the candidate x = -4 is rejected because
options: It does not satisfy the original equation after squaring
mcqs.why: Checking in the original equation: for x = -4 the left side is √(-20 + 21) = √1 = 1 while the right side is -4 + 3 = -1. Since 1 ≠ -1, x = -4 is an extraneous root produced by squaring.
Square both sides: 2x - 1 = x² - 4x + 4, so x² - 6x + 5 = (x - 5)(x - 1) = 0, giving x = 5 or x = 1. Check x = 1: √1 = 1 but 1 - 2 = -1, so it is extraneous; only x = 5 remains.
Square both sides: 29 - 4x = 4x² + 12x + 9, so x² + 4x - 5 = (x + 5)(x - 1) = 0, giving x = -5 or x = 1. Check x = -5: √49 = 7 but 2(-5) + 3 = -7, so it is extraneous; only x = 1 remains.

Squaring and isolating gives √((x + 7)(x + 2)) = 2x + 2; squaring again gives 3x² - x - 10 = (x - 2)(3x + 5) = 0, so x = 2 or x = -5/3. For x = -5/3 a square root would equal the negative number -4/3, so it is extraneous; only x = 2 remains.
Squaring twice leads to 11x² + 4x = x(11x + 4) = 0, so x = 0 or x = -4/11. The equation is defined only for x ≥ 0 because of √(x), so x = -4/11 is rejected and the solution set is {0}.

Isolate and square twice to get 3x² + 2x - 56 = 0. Formula: x = (-2 ± √(4 + 672)) / 6 = (-2 ± 26) / 6, giving x = 4 or x = -14/3. For x = -14/3 the left side is negative while the right side is positive, so only x = 4 remains.
Let u = x² + 2x: isolating and squaring gives 10√(u + 4) = 20, so √(u + 4) = 2 and u = 0. Then x² + 2x = x(x + 2) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = -2, and both values check in the original equation.
Let u = 2x² + 3x: isolating and squaring gives 4√(u + 1) = 0, so u = -1. Then 2x² + 3x + 1 = (x + 1)(2x + 1) = 0, giving x = -1 or x = -1/2, and both values check.

mcqs.q: If x satisfies √(40 - 9x) - 2√(7 - x) = √(-x), then 2x + 5 equals
mcqs.why: Isolating, squaring twice and simplifying gives 3 - x = √(x² - 7x); squaring again: 9 - 6x + x² = x² - 7x, so 9 = -x and x = -9, which checks. Then 2x + 5 = 2(-9) + 5 = -18 + 5 = -13.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • (x + 1)(x - 5) = 0 has solutions x = -1 and x = 5 by the zero-product property.
  • Before applying the quadratic formula, an equation must be in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0; 2x² - x = 3 becomes 2x² - x - 3 = 0.
  • x² - 3x - 4 = 0 has solutions 4 and -1; x² + 7x - 18 = 0 has solutions 2 and -9.
  • x² - 1/4 = 0 gives x = ±1/2.
  • 2w⁴ - 5w² + 2 = 0 is solved by the substitution y = w², giving w = ±√2, ±1/√2.
  • If x = -1 and x = 1 are both solutions of ax² + bx + 2 = 0, then a = -2 and b = 0.
  • 49x² - 316x + 132 = 0 factorises as (x - 6)(49x - 22) = 0, with solutions 6 and 22/49.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). If (x + 1)(x - 5) = 0, then the solutions are

Options: (a) x = 1, -5 (b) x = 1, 5 (c) x = -1, -5 (d) x = -1, 5

Correct answer: x = -1, 5

Q: Q1(ii). If x² - x - 1 = 0, then x =

Options: (a) (-1 ± √5)/(2) (b) -1 ± (√5)/(2) (c) (1 ± √5)/(2) (d) 1 ± (√5)/(2)

Correct answer: (1 ± √5)/(2)

Q: Q1(iii). (-1 ± √5)/(2) in simplified form is

Options: (a) 1 ± √24 (b) 1 ± √6 (c) 2 ± √6 (d) cannot be simplified

Correct answer: cannot be simplified

Q: Q1(iv). To apply the quadratic formula to 2x² - x = 3

Options: (a) a = 2, b = -1, c = 3 (b) a = 2, b = 1, c = 3 (c) a = 2, b = -1, c = -3 (d) a = 2, b = -1, c = 0

Correct answer: a = 2, b = -1, c = -3

Q: Q1(v). If x² - 3x - 4 = 0, then the solutions are

Options: (a) x = 4, -1 (b) x = -4, 1 (c) x = 4, 1 (d) x = -4, -1

Correct answer: x = 4, -1

Q: Q1(vi). If 2x² + 4x - 9 = 0, the solutions are

Options: (a) x = (2 ± √22)/(2) (b) x = (-2 ± √22)/(2) (c) x = 2 ± (√22)/(2) (d) x = -2 ± (√22)/(2)

Correct answer: x = (-2 ± √22)/(2)

Q: Q1(vii). x² - (1)/(4) = 0, the solutions are

Options: (a) x = ±(1)/(2) (b) x = ±(1)/(4) (c) x = ±(1)/(8) (d) x = ±(1)/(16)

Correct answer: x = ±(1)/(2)

Q: Q1(viii). What are the solutions of the equation x² + 7x - 18 = 0?

Options: (a) 2 or -9 (b) -2 or 9 (c) -2 or -9 (d) 2 or 9

Correct answer: 2 or -9

Q: Q1(ix). Which of the following values of x are roots of the equation x² - 8x + 15 = 0?

Options: (a) x = 1 or x = -7 (b) x = 2 or x = 4 (c) x = -2 or x = 4 (d) x = 3 or x = 5

Correct answer: x = 3 or x = 5

Q: Q2. Solve 2w⁴ - 5w² + 2 = 0

Ans: By substitution:
Let y = w², so w⁴ = y².
The equation becomes:
2y² - 5y + 2 = 0
By factorization, split -5y into -4y - y:
2y² - 4y - y + 2 = 0
2y(y - 2) - 1(y - 2) = 0
(y - 2)(2y - 1) = 0
y = 2 or y = (1)/(2)
Substitute back y = w²:
w² = 2 or w² = (1)/(2)
w = ±√2 or w = ±(1)/(√2)
Solution set: {±√2, ±(1)/(√2)}

Q: Q3. Find the constants a and b such that x = -1 and x = 1 are both solutions to the equation ax² + bx + 2 = 0

Ans: Substitute x = -1 in the equation, since it is a solution:
a(-1)² + b(-1) + 2 = 0
a - b + 2 = 0 ... (1)
Substitute x = 1 in the equation, since it is also a solution:
a(1)² + b(1) + 2 = 0
a + b + 2 = 0 ... (2)
Add equations (1) and (2):
2a + 4 = 0
a = -2
Substitute a = -2 in equation (2):
-2 + b + 2 = 0
b = 0
Check: with a = -2 and b = 0 the equation is -2x² + 2 = 0, i.e. x² = 1, whose solutions are x = 1 and x = -1 (true)
Answer: a = -2, b = 0

Q: Q4. Find all values of x such that x² + 5x + 6 and x² + 19x + 34 are equal

Ans: Set the two expressions equal:
x² + 5x + 6 = x² + 19x + 34
Subtract x² from both sides:
5x + 6 = 19x + 34
Bring the x-terms to one side and the constants to the other:
5x - 19x = 34 - 6
-14x = 28
Divide both sides by -14:
x = -2
Check: for x = -2: 4 - 10 + 6 = 0 and 4 - 38 + 34 = 0, so the two expressions are equal (both 0)
Answer: x = -2

Q: Q5. Find the solutions to the equation: 49x² - 316x + 132 = 0

Ans: By factorization:
49x² - 316x + 132 = 0
Split the middle term -316x into -294x - 22x, because (-294) × (-22) = 6468 = 49 × 132 and -294 + (-22) = -316:
49x² - 294x - 22x + 132 = 0
49x(x - 6) - 22(x - 6) = 0
(x - 6)(49x - 22) = 0
By the zero-product property:
x - 6 = 0 or 49x - 22 = 0
x = 6 or x = (22)/(49)
Check: for x = 6: 49(36) - 316(6) + 132 = 1764 - 1896 + 132 = 0 (true)
Solution set: {6, (22)/(49)}

mcqs.why: By the zero-product property, x + 1 = 0 or x - 5 = 0. Solving each factor: x = -1 from the first and x = 5 from the second, so the solutions are x = -1, 5.

Q1(iii). (-1 ± √5)/(2) in simplified form is
mcqs.why: The numerator -1 ± √5 shares no common factor with the denominator 2, and √5 cannot be reduced, so the expression (-1 ± √5) / 2 is already in its simplest form.

mcqs.q: Q1(iv). To apply the quadratic formula to 2x² - x = 3
mcqs.why: First write the equation in standard form by moving 3 to the left: 2x² - x - 3 = 0. Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0 gives a = 2, b = -1 and c = -3.

mcqs.q: Q1(v). If x² - 3x - 4 = 0, then the solutions are
mcqs.why: Split -3x as -4x + x: x² - 4x + x - 4 = x(x - 4) + 1(x - 4) = (x - 4)(x + 1) = 0, so x - 4 = 0 or x + 1 = 0, giving x = 4 or x = -1.

mcqs.q: Q1(vi). If 2x² + 4x - 9 = 0, the solutions are
Q1(vii). x² - (1)/(4) = 0, the solutions are
mcqs.why: Rewrite as x² = 1/4 and take the square root of both sides: x = ±√(1/4) = ±(1/2), since (1/2)² = 1/4.

mcqs.q: Q1(viii). What are the solutions of the equation x² + 7x - 18 = 0?
Q1(ix). Which of the following values of x are roots of the equation x² - 8x + 15 = 0?
mcqs.why: Formula with a = 1, b = -8, c = 15: x = (8 ± √(64 - 60)) / 2 = (8 ± 2) / 2, giving x = 10/2 = 5 or x = 6/2 = 3, so the roots are x = 3 or x = 5.

mcqs.q: Solve 2w⁴ - 5w² + 2 = 0.
mcqs.why: Let y = w²: 2y² - 5y + 2 = (y - 2)(2y - 1) = 0, so y = 2 or y = 1/2. Substituting back, w² = 2 gives w = ±√2 and w² = 1/2 gives w = ±(1)/(√2).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The discriminant of ax² + bx + c = 0 is b² - 4ac.
  • Discriminant > 0 gives real unequal roots (rational if it is a perfect square, otherwise irrational); = 0 gives real equal roots; < 0 gives imaginary unequal roots.
  • Discriminants: x² - 4x + 13 → -36; 4x² - 5x + 1 → 9; x² + x + 1 → -3.
  • Roots are equal exactly when b² - 4ac = 0: x² + kx + 9 needs k = ±6, and x² - 5x + k needs k = 25/4.
  • For 2x² + 3x + k = 0 the roots are real when k ≤ 9/8 and imaginary when k > 9/8.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation: x² - 4x + 13 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is b² - 4ac.
Comparing x² - 4x + 13 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = -4, c = 13
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (-4)² - 4(1)(13)
= 16 - 52
= -36
Answer: -36

Q: Q1(ii). Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation: 4x² - 5x + 1 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is b² - 4ac.
Comparing 4x² - 5x + 1 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 4, b = -5, c = 1
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (-5)² - 4(4)(1)
= 25 - 16
= 9
Answer: 9

Q: Q1(iii). Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation: x² + x + 1 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is b² - 4ac.
Comparing x² + x + 1 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = 1, c = 1
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (1)² - 4(1)(1)
= 1 - 4
= -3
Answer: -3

Q: Q2(i). Examine the nature of the roots of the equation: 3x² - 5x + 1 = 0

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: if b² - 4ac > 0 the roots are real and unequal (rational if b² - 4ac is a perfect square, otherwise irrational); if b² - 4ac = 0 the roots are real and equal; if b² - 4ac < 0 the roots are imaginary and unequal.
Comparing 3x² - 5x + 1 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 3, b = -5, c = 1
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (-5)² - 4(3)(1)
= 25 - 12
= 13
Since the discriminant is positive but not a perfect square, the roots are real, unequal and irrational.
Answer: Real (irrational) and unequal

Q: Q2(ii). Examine the nature of the roots of the equation: 6x² + x - 2 = 0

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: if b² - 4ac > 0 the roots are real and unequal (rational if b² - 4ac is a perfect square, otherwise irrational); if b² - 4ac = 0 the roots are real and equal; if b² - 4ac < 0 the roots are imaginary and unequal.
Comparing 6x² + x - 2 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 6, b = 1, c = -2
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (1)² - 4(6)(-2)
= 1 + 48
= 49 = (7)²
Since the discriminant is positive and a perfect square, the roots are real, unequal and rational.
Answer: Real (rational) and unequal

Q: Q2(iii). Examine the nature of the roots of the equation: 3x² + 2x + 1 = 0

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: if b² - 4ac > 0 the roots are real and unequal (rational if b² - 4ac is a perfect square, otherwise irrational); if b² - 4ac = 0 the roots are real and equal; if b² - 4ac < 0 the roots are imaginary and unequal.
Comparing 3x² + 2x + 1 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 3, b = 2, c = 1
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (2)² - 4(3)(1)
= 4 - 12
= -8
Since the discriminant is negative, the roots are imaginary and unequal.
Answer: Complex (imaginary) and unequal

Q: Q3(i). For what value of k are the roots of the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 equal?

Ans: The roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 are equal if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac = 0.
Comparing x² + kx + 9 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = k, c = 9
For equal roots, b² - 4ac = 0
⇒ (k)² - 4(1)(9) = 0
⇒ k² - 36 = 0
⇒ k² = 36
⇒ k = ±6
Answer: k = ±6

Q: Q3(ii). For what value of k are the roots of the equation 12x² + kx + 3 = 0 equal?

Ans: The roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 are equal if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac = 0.
Comparing 12x² + kx + 3 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 12, b = k, c = 3
For equal roots, b² - 4ac = 0
⇒ (k)² - 4(12)(3) = 0
⇒ k² - 144 = 0
⇒ k² = 144
⇒ k = ±12
Answer: k = ±12

Q: Q3(iii). For what value of k are the roots of the equation x² - 5x + k = 0 equal?

Ans: The roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 are equal if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac = 0.
Comparing x² - 5x + k = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = -5, c = k
For equal roots, b² - 4ac = 0
⇒ (-5)² - 4(1)(k) = 0
⇒ 25 - 4k = 0
⇒ 4k = 25
⇒ k = (25)/(4)
Answer: k = (25)/(4)

Q: Q4(i). Determine whether the quadratic equation x² + 5x + 5 = 0 has real roots and if so, find the roots.

Ans: The equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has real roots if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac ≥ 0, and then the roots are given by the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a).
Comparing x² + 5x + 5 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = 5, c = 5
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (5)² - 4(1)(5)
= 25 - 20
= 5
Since the discriminant is positive, the roots are real.
By the quadratic formula, x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a)
x = (-5 ± √(5))/(2(1))
x = (-5 ± √(5))/(2)
Answer: The roots are real and are (-5 + √(5))/(2) and (-5 - √(5))/(2)

Q: Q4(ii). Determine whether the quadratic equation 4x² + 12x + 9 = 0 has real roots and if so, find the roots.

Ans: The equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has real roots if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac ≥ 0; if b² - 4ac = 0 the two roots are real and equal.
Comparing 4x² + 12x + 9 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 4, b = 12, c = 9
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (12)² - 4(4)(9)
= 144 - 144
= 0
Since the discriminant is zero, the roots are real and equal.
Now solve by factorization:
4x² + 12x + 9 = 0
(2x + 3)(2x + 3) = 0
(2x + 3)² = 0
⇒ 2x + 3 = 0
⇒ x = -(3)/(2)
Answer: The roots are real and equal, x = -(3)/(2), -(3)/(2)

Q: Q4(iii). Determine whether the quadratic equation 6x² + x - 2 = 0 has real roots and if so, find the roots.

Ans: The equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has real roots if and only if the discriminant b² - 4ac ≥ 0.
Comparing 6x² + x - 2 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 6, b = 1, c = -2
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (1)² - 4(6)(-2)
= 1 + 48
= 49
Since the discriminant is positive, the roots are real.
Now solve by factorization:
6x² + x - 2 = 0
6x² + 4x - 3x - 2 = 0
2x(3x + 2) - 1(3x + 2) = 0
(3x + 2)(2x - 1) = 0
⇒ 3x + 2 = 0 or 2x - 1 = 0
⇒ x = -(2)/(3) or x = (1)/(2)
Answer: The roots are real and are (1)/(2) and -(2)/(3)

Q: Q5(i). Determine the nature of roots of the quadratic equation 3x² - 10x + 3 = 0 and verify the result by solving it.

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: positive and a perfect square means real, rational and unequal roots; positive but not a perfect square means real, irrational and unequal roots; zero means real and equal roots; negative means imaginary roots.
Comparing 3x² - 10x + 3 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 3, b = -10, c = 3
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (-10)² - 4(3)(3)
= 100 - 36
= 64 = (8)²
Since the discriminant is positive and a perfect square, the roots should be real, rational and unequal.
Verification by solving:
3x² - 10x + 3 = 0
3x² - 9x - x + 3 = 0
3x(x - 3) - 1(x - 3) = 0
(x - 3)(3x - 1) = 0
⇒ x - 3 = 0 or 3x - 1 = 0
⇒ x = 3 or x = (1)/(3)
The roots 3 and (1)/(3) are real, rational and unequal, so the result is verified.
Answer: The roots are real (rational) and unequal: 3, (1)/(3)

Q: Q5(ii). Determine the nature of roots of the quadratic equation x² - 6x + 4 = 0 and verify the result by solving it.

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: positive and a perfect square means real, rational and unequal roots; positive but not a perfect square means real, irrational and unequal roots; zero means real and equal roots; negative means imaginary roots.
Comparing x² - 6x + 4 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = -6, c = 4
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (-6)² - 4(1)(4)
= 36 - 16
= 20
Since the discriminant is positive but not a perfect square, the roots should be real, irrational and unequal.
Verification by solving with the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a):
x = (6 ± √(20))/(2(1))
x = (6 ± 2√(5))/(2)
x = 3 ± √(5)
The roots 3 + √(5) and 3 - √(5) are real, irrational and unequal, so the result is verified.
Answer: The roots are real (irrational) and unequal: 3 + √(5), 3 - √(5)

Q: Q5(iii). Determine the nature of roots of the quadratic equation x² - 3 = 0 and verify the result by solving it.

Ans: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b² - 4ac: positive and a perfect square means real, rational and unequal roots; positive but not a perfect square means real, irrational and unequal roots; zero means real and equal roots; negative means imaginary roots.
Comparing x² - 3 = 0, i.e. x² + 0x - 3 = 0, with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = 0, c = -3
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (0)² - 4(1)(-3)
= 0 + 12
= 12
Since the discriminant is positive but not a perfect square, the roots should be real, irrational and unequal.
Verification by solving:
x² - 3 = 0
x² = 3
x = ±√(3)
The roots √(3) and -√(3) are real, irrational and unequal, so the result is verified.
Answer: The roots are real (irrational) and unequal: √(3), -√(3)

Q: Q6(i). For what value of k are the roots of the equation 2x² + 3x + k = 0 (a) real (b) imaginary?

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are real if b² - 4ac ≥ 0 and imaginary if b² - 4ac < 0.
Comparing 2x² + 3x + k = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 2, b = 3, c = k
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (3)² - 4(2)(k)
= 9 - 8k
(a) For real roots, discriminant ≥ 0
⇒ 9 - 8k ≥ 0
⇒ 9 ≥ 8k
⇒ k ≤ (9)/(8)
(b) For imaginary roots, discriminant < 0
⇒ 9 - 8k < 0
⇒ 9 < 8k
⇒ k > (9)/(8)
Answer: (a) k ≤ (9)/(8) (b) k > (9)/(8)

Q: Q6(ii). For what value of k are the roots of the equation kx² + 2x + 1 = 0 (a) real (b) imaginary?

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are real if b² - 4ac ≥ 0 and imaginary if b² - 4ac < 0.
Comparing kx² + 2x + 1 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = k, b = 2, c = 1
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (2)² - 4(k)(1)
= 4 - 4k
(a) For real roots, discriminant ≥ 0
⇒ 4 - 4k ≥ 0
⇒ 4 ≥ 4k
⇒ k ≤ 1
(b) For imaginary roots, discriminant < 0
⇒ 4 - 4k < 0
⇒ 4 < 4k
⇒ k > 1
Answer: (a) k ≤ 1 (b) k > 1

Q: Q6(iii). For what value of k are the roots of the equation x² + 5x + k = 0 (a) real (b) imaginary?

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are real if b² - 4ac ≥ 0 and imaginary if b² - 4ac < 0.
Comparing x² + 5x + k = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 1, b = 5, c = k
Discriminant = b² - 4ac
= (5)² - 4(1)(k)
= 25 - 4k
(a) For real roots, discriminant ≥ 0
⇒ 25 - 4k ≥ 0
⇒ 25 ≥ 4k
⇒ k ≤ (25)/(4)
(b) For imaginary roots, discriminant < 0
⇒ 25 - 4k < 0
⇒ 25 < 4k
⇒ k > (25)/(4)
Answer: (a) k ≤ (25)/(4) (b) k > (25)/(4)

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of x² - 4x + 13 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 1, b = -4, c = 13: substitute to get (-4)² - 4(1)(13) = 16 - 52 = -36.

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of 4x² - 5x + 1 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 4, b = -5, c = 1: substitute to get (-5)² - 4(4)(1) = 25 - 16 = 9.

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of x² + x + 1 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = b² - 4ac with a = 1, b = 1, c = 1: substitute to get (1)² - 4(1)(1) = 1 - 4 = -3.

mcqs.q: Examine the nature of the roots of 3x² - 5x + 1 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = (-5)² - 4(3)(1) = 25 - 12 = 13. Since 13 is positive but not a perfect square, the roots are real, unequal and irrational.

mcqs.q: Examine the nature of the roots of 6x² + x - 2 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = (1)² - 4(6)(-2) = 1 + 48 = 49 = 7². Since 49 is positive and a perfect square, the roots are real, unequal and rational.

mcqs.q: Examine the nature of the roots of 3x² + 2x + 1 = 0.
mcqs.why: Discriminant = (2)² - 4(3)(1) = 4 - 12 = -8. Since the discriminant is negative, the roots are complex (imaginary) and unequal.

mcqs.q: For what values of k are the roots of x² + kx + 9 = 0 equal?
mcqs.why: Equal roots need discriminant zero: k² - 4(1)(9) = 0, so k² - 36 = 0, hence k² = 36 and taking square roots gives k = ±6.

mcqs.q: For what value of k are the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0 equal?
mcqs.why: Equal roots need discriminant zero: (-5)² - 4(1)(k) = 0, so 25 - 4k = 0, hence 4k = 25 and dividing by 4 gives k = 25/4.

mcqs.q: The roots of x² + 5x + 5 = 0 are
mcqs.why: Discriminant = 25 - 4(1)(5) = 5 > 0, so the roots are real. Formula: x = (-5 ± √5) / (2 × 1) = (-5 ± √5) / 2.

mcqs.q: For 2x² + 3x + k = 0, the roots are imaginary when
mcqs.why: Discriminant = 3² - 4(2)(k) = 9 - 8k. Imaginary roots need discriminant < 0: 9 - 8k < 0, so 9 < 8k and dividing by 8 gives k > 9/8.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The complex cube roots of unity are ω = (-1 + i√3)/2 and ω² = (-1 - i√3)/2, where i = √(-1).
  • The key properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
  • The cube roots of -1 are -1, -ω, -ω²; of 8 are 2, 2ω, 2ω²; of -27 are -3, -3ω, -3ω².
  • Powers of ω are reduced by writing the exponent as a multiple of 3 plus a remainder.
  • -1 + i√3 = 2ω and -1 - i√3 = 2ω².
  • x³ - y³ = (x - y)(x - ωy)(x - ω²y).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the cube roots of the number: -1

Ans: Let x be a cube root of -1.
Then x = ∛(-1)
⇒ x³ = -1
⇒ x³ + 1 = 0
⇒ (x + 1)(x² - x + 1) = 0
⇒ x + 1 = 0 or x² - x + 1 = 0
From x + 1 = 0, x = -1
From x² - x + 1 = 0, by the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a) with a = 1, b = -1, c = 1:
x = (1 ± √(1 - 4))/(2)
x = (1 ± √(-3))/(2)
x = (1 ± i√(3))/(2), where i = √(-1)
Now ω = (-1 + i√(3))/(2) and ω² = (-1 - i√(3))/(2), so (1 - i√(3))/(2) = -ω and (1 + i√(3))/(2) = -ω²
Answer: The cube roots of -1 are -1, -ω, -ω²

Q: Q1(ii). Find the cube roots of the number: 8

Ans: Let x be a cube root of 8.
Then x = ∛(8)
⇒ x³ = 8
⇒ x³ - 8 = 0
⇒ (x - 2)(x² + 2x + 4) = 0
⇒ x - 2 = 0 or x² + 2x + 4 = 0
From x - 2 = 0, x = 2
From x² + 2x + 4 = 0, by the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a) with a = 1, b = 2, c = 4:
x = (-2 ± √(4 - 16))/(2)
x = (-2 ± √(-12))/(2)
x = (-2 ± 2i√(3))/(2)
x = -1 ± i√(3), where i = √(-1)
Now -1 + i√(3) = 2ω and -1 - i√(3) = 2ω², because ω = (-1 + i√(3))/(2) and ω² = (-1 - i√(3))/(2)
Answer: The cube roots of 8 are 2, 2ω, 2ω²

Q: Q1(iii). Find the cube roots of the number: -27

Ans: Let x be a cube root of -27.
Then x = ∛(-27)
⇒ x³ = -27
⇒ x³ + 27 = 0
⇒ (x + 3)(x² - 3x + 9) = 0
⇒ x + 3 = 0 or x² - 3x + 9 = 0
From x + 3 = 0, x = -3
From x² - 3x + 9 = 0, by the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac))/(2a) with a = 1, b = -3, c = 9:
x = (3 ± √(9 - 36))/(2)
x = (3 ± √(-27))/(2)
x = (3 ± 3i√(3))/(2), where i = √(-1)
Now (3 - 3i√(3))/(2) = -3ω and (3 + 3i√(3))/(2) = -3ω², because ω = (-1 + i√(3))/(2) and ω² = (-1 - i√(3))/(2)
Answer: The cube roots of -27 are -3, -3ω, -3ω²

Q: Q2(i). Evaluate: ω¹² + ω⁵⁸ + ω⁹⁵

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
Reduce each power by writing the exponent as a multiple of 3 plus a remainder.
ω¹² = (ω³)⁴
= (1)⁴
= 1
ω⁵⁸ = ω⁵⁷ · ω
= (ω³)¹⁹ · ω
= (1)¹⁹ · ω
= ω
ω⁹⁵ = ω⁹³ · ω²
= (ω³)³¹ · ω²
= (1)³¹ · ω²
= ω²
∴ ω¹² + ω⁵⁸ + ω⁹⁵ = 1 + ω + ω²
= 0 (by the property 1 + ω + ω² = 0)
Answer: 0

Q: Q2(ii). Evaluate: (1 + ω - ω²)⁷

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so 1 + ω = -ω².
1 + ω - ω² = -ω² - ω² (replacing 1 + ω by -ω²)
= -2ω²
∴ (1 + ω - ω²)⁷ = (-2ω²)⁷
= (-2)⁷ · (ω²)⁷
= -128 · ω¹⁴
Now ω¹⁴ = ω¹² · ω²
= (ω³)⁴ · ω²
= (1)⁴ · ω²
= ω²
∴ (1 + ω - ω²)⁷ = -128ω²
Answer: -128ω²

Q: Q2(iii). Evaluate: (1 + 3ω - ω²)(1 + ω - 2ω²)

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so ω² = -1 - ω.
First factor: 1 + 3ω - ω² = 1 + 3ω - (-1 - ω)
= 1 + 3ω + 1 + ω
= 2 + 4ω
Second factor: 1 + ω - 2ω² = 1 + ω - 2(-1 - ω)
= 1 + ω + 2 + 2ω
= 3 + 3ω
Multiply the two factors:
(2 + 4ω)(3 + 3ω) = 6 + 6ω + 12ω + 12ω²
= 6 + 18ω + 12ω²
Replace ω² by -1 - ω:
= 6 + 18ω + 12(-1 - ω)
= 6 + 18ω - 12 - 12ω
= -6 + 6ω
= 6(ω - 1)
Answer: 6(ω - 1)

Q: Q3(i). Prove that: (1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²)(1 - ω - ω²) = 6

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so ω + ω² = -1.
First simplify the third factor:
1 - ω - ω² = 1 - (ω + ω²)
= 1 - (-1)
= 2
Now multiply the first two factors:
(1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²) = 1 + 2ω² + 2ω + 4ω³
= 1 + 2(ω + ω²) + 4ω³
= 1 + 2(-1) + 4(1) (using ω + ω² = -1 and ω³ = 1)
= 1 - 2 + 4
= 3
∴ L.H.S. = (1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²)(1 - ω - ω²)
= 3 × 2
= 6
= R.H.S.
Answer: (1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²)(1 - ω - ω²) = 6, proved

Q: Q3(ii). Prove that: (-1 + i√(3))⁴(-1 - i√(3))⁵ = 512ω²

Ans: The complex cube roots of unity are ω = (-1 + i√(3))/(2) and ω² = (-1 - i√(3))/(2), and ω³ = 1.
∴ -1 + i√(3) = 2ω
and -1 - i√(3) = 2ω²
L.H.S. = (-1 + i√(3))⁴(-1 - i√(3))⁵
= (2ω)⁴(2ω²)⁵
= 16ω⁴ · 32ω¹⁰
= 512ω¹⁴
Now ω¹⁴ = ω¹² · ω²
= (ω³)⁴ · ω²
= (1)⁴ · ω²
= ω²
∴ L.H.S. = 512ω²
= R.H.S.
Answer: (-1 + i√(3))⁴(-1 - i√(3))⁵ = 512ω², proved

Q: Q4(i). Show that: x³ - y³ = (x - y)(x - ωy)(x - ω²y)

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so ω + ω² = -1.
R.H.S. = (x - y)(x - ωy)(x - ω²y)
First multiply the last two factors:
(x - ωy)(x - ω²y) = x² - ω²xy - ωxy + ω³y²
= x² - (ω + ω²)xy + ω³y²
= x² - (-1)xy + (1)y² (using ω + ω² = -1 and ω³ = 1)
= x² + xy + y²
∴ R.H.S. = (x - y)(x² + xy + y²)
= x³ + x²y + xy² - x²y - xy² - y³
= x³ - y³
= L.H.S.
Answer: x³ - y³ = (x - y)(x - ωy)(x - ω²y), proved

Q: Q4(ii). Show that: (1 + ω)(1 + ω²)(1 + ω⁴)(1 + ω⁸) = 1

Ans: For the complex cube root of unity ω, the properties are ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so 1 + ω = -ω² and 1 + ω² = -ω.
Reduce the higher powers using ω³ = 1:
ω⁴ = ω³ · ω = 1 · ω = ω
ω⁸ = ω⁶ · ω² = (ω³)² · ω² = 1 · ω² = ω²
∴ (1 + ω⁴) = (1 + ω) and (1 + ω⁸) = (1 + ω²)
L.H.S. = (1 + ω)(1 + ω²)(1 + ω)(1 + ω²)
= [(1 + ω)(1 + ω²)] · [(1 + ω)(1 + ω²)]
Now (1 + ω)(1 + ω²) = (-ω²)(-ω) (using 1 + ω = -ω² and 1 + ω² = -ω)
= ω³
= 1
∴ L.H.S. = 1 × 1
= 1
= R.H.S.
Answer: (1 + ω)(1 + ω²)(1 + ω⁴)(1 + ω⁸) = 1, proved

mcqs.q: The cube roots of -1 are
mcqs.why: Set x³ = -1, so x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² - x + 1) = 0. Then x = -1, or by the formula x = (1 ± √(-3)) / 2 = (1 ± i√3) / 2, which are -ω and -ω².

mcqs.q: The cube roots of 8 are
mcqs.why: Set x³ = 8, so x³ - 8 = (x - 2)(x² + 2x + 4) = 0. Then x = 2, or by the formula x = (-2 ± √(-12)) / 2 = -1 ± i√3, which are 2ω and 2ω².

mcqs.q: The cube roots of -27 are
mcqs.why: Set x³ = -27, so x³ + 27 = (x + 3)(x² - 3x + 9) = 0. Then x = -3, or by the formula x = (3 ± √(-27)) / 2 = (3 ± 3i√3) / 2, which are -3ω and -3ω².

mcqs.q: The value of ω³, where ω is a complex cube root of unity, is
mcqs.why: By the defining property of the cube roots of unity, ω is a root of x³ = 1 other than 1 itself, so ω³ = 1. This is used to reduce every higher power of ω.

mcqs.q: The value of 1 + ω + ω² is
mcqs.why: Since ω satisfies ω² + ω + 1 = 0 (from x³ - 1 = (x - 1)(x² + x + 1) with ω ≠ 1), rearranging that equation directly gives 1 + ω + ω² = 0.

mcqs.q: Evaluate ω¹² + ω⁵⁸ + ω⁹⁵.
mcqs.why: Reduce each power using ω³ = 1: ω¹² = (ω³)⁴ = 1, ω⁵⁸ = (ω³)¹⁹ · ω = ω, and ω⁹⁵ = (ω³)³¹ · ω² = ω². The sum is 1 + ω + ω² = 0.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (1 + ω - ω²)⁷.
mcqs.why: Since 1 + ω = -ω², the base is -ω² - ω² = -2ω². Then (-2ω²)⁷ = (-2)⁷ · ω¹⁴ = -128 · ω², because ω¹⁴ = (ω³)⁴ · ω² = ω².

mcqs.q: Evaluate (1 + 3ω - ω²)(1 + ω - 2ω²).
mcqs.why: Replace ω² by -1 - ω: the first factor becomes 2 + 4ω and the second becomes 3 + 3ω. Multiplying: 6 + 18ω + 12ω² = 6 + 18ω + 12(-1 - ω) = -6 + 6ω = 6(ω - 1).

mcqs.q: The expression -1 + i√3 in terms of ω equals
mcqs.why: By definition ω = (-1 + i√3) / 2. Multiplying both sides by 2 gives 2ω = -1 + i√3, so -1 + i√3 is exactly twice the cube root ω.

mcqs.q: In the proof of (1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²)(1 - ω - ω²) = 6, the factor (1 - ω - ω²) simplifies to
mcqs.why: Since 1 + ω + ω² = 0, we have ω + ω² = -1. Substitute: 1 - ω - ω² = 1 - (ω + ω²) = 1 - (-1) = 2, and the remaining product (1 + 2ω)(1 + 2ω²) = 3, giving 3 × 2 = 6.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β: α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a.
  • α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ and (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ.
  • For 4x² - 4x - 3 = 0: sum = 1, product = -3/4; for 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0: sum = -5/2, product = 3.
  • If the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0 differ by unity, then 25 - 4k = 1, so k = 6.
  • If sum and product of the roots of mx² - 3x - n = 0 are both 3/5, then m = 5 and n = -3.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Without solving the equation, find the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation: 4x² - 4x - 3 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing 4x² - 4x - 3 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 4, b = -4, c = -3
Sum of the roots = -b/a
= -(-4)/(4)
= (4)/(4)
= 1
Product of the roots = c/a
= (-3)/(4)
= -(3)/(4)
Answer: Sum of the roots = 1, Product of the roots = -(3)/(4)

Q: Q1(ii). Without solving the equation, find the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation: 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 2, b = 5, c = 6
Sum of the roots = -b/a
= -(5)/(2)
= -(5)/(2)
Product of the roots = c/a
= (6)/(2)
= 3
Answer: Sum of the roots = -(5)/(2), Product of the roots = 3

Q: Q1(iii). Without solving the equation, find the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation: 3x² + 2x - 5 = 0

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing 3x² + 2x - 5 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 3, b = 2, c = -5
Sum of the roots = -b/a
= -(2)/(3)
= -(2)/(3)
Product of the roots = c/a
= (-5)/(3)
= -(5)/(3)
Answer: Sum of the roots = -(2)/(3), Product of the roots = -(5)/(3)

Q: Q2. Find the value of k if sum of the roots of 2x² + kx + 6 = 0 is equal to the product of its roots.

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing 2x² + kx + 6 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have
a = 2, b = k, c = 6
Sum of the roots = -b/a
= -(k)/(2)
Product of the roots = c/a
= (6)/(2)
= 3
Given condition: sum of the roots = product of the roots
⇒ -(k)/(2) = 3
⇒ -k = 6
⇒ k = -6
Answer: k = -6

Q: Q3. Find the value of k if the sum of the square of the roots of x² - 5kx + 6k² = 0 is equal to 13.

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a, and α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ.
Let α, β be the roots of x² - 5kx + 6k² = 0.
Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have a = 1, b = -5k, c = 6k²
α + β = -b/a
= -(-5k)/(1)
= 5k
αβ = c/a
= (6k²)/(1)
= 6k²
Given condition: α² + β² = 13
⇒ (α + β)² - 2αβ = 13
⇒ (5k)² - 2(6k²) = 13
⇒ 25k² - 12k² = 13
⇒ 13k² = 13
⇒ k² = 1
⇒ k = ±1
Answer: k = ±1

Q: Q4. Find the value of k if the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0 differ by unity.

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a, and (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ.
Let α, β be the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0.
Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have a = 1, b = -5, c = k
α + β = -b/a
= -(-5)/(1)
= 5
αβ = c/a
= (k)/(1)
= k
Given condition: the roots differ by unity, so α - β = 1 (taking α > β)
⇒ (α - β)² = 1
⇒ (α + β)² - 4αβ = 1
⇒ (5)² - 4(k) = 1
⇒ 25 - 4k = 1
⇒ 4k = 24
⇒ k = 6
Answer: k = 6

Q: Q5. Find the value of k if the roots of x² - 9x + k + 2 = 0 differ by three.

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a, and (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ.
Let α, β be the roots of x² - 9x + k + 2 = 0.
Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have a = 1, b = -9, c = k + 2
α + β = -b/a
= -(-9)/(1)
= 9
αβ = c/a
= (k + 2)/(1)
= k + 2
Given condition: the roots differ by three, so α - β = 3 (taking α > β)
⇒ (α - β)² = 9
⇒ (α + β)² - 4αβ = 9
⇒ (9)² - 4(k + 2) = 9
⇒ 81 - 4k - 8 = 9
⇒ 73 - 4k = 9
⇒ 4k = 64
⇒ k = 16
Answer: k = 16

Q: Q6. If α, β are the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0, find k such that 3α + 2β = 12.

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing x² - 5x + k = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have a = 1, b = -5, c = k
α + β = -b/a
= -(-5)/(1)
= 5 ... (i)
αβ = c/a
= (k)/(1)
= k ... (ii)
Also given: 3α + 2β = 12 ... (iii)
Multiply (i) by 2:
2α + 2β = 10 ... (iv)
Subtract (iv) from (iii):
(3α + 2β) - (2α + 2β) = 12 - 10
⇒ α = 2
Put α = 2 in (i):
2 + β = 5
⇒ β = 3
Put α = 2 and β = 3 in (ii):
k = αβ
= (2)(3)
= 6
Answer: k = 6

Q: Q7. Find the value of m and n if both sum and product of roots of the equation mx² - 3x - n = 0 are equal to (3)/(5).

Ans: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β, sum of roots α + β = -b/a and product of roots αβ = c/a.
Comparing mx² - 3x - n = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we have a = m, b = -3, c = -n
Sum of the roots = -b/a
= -(-3)/(m)
= (3)/(m)
Product of the roots = c/a
= (-n)/(m)
Given condition: sum of the roots = (3)/(5)
⇒ (3)/(m) = (3)/(5)
⇒ m = 5
Given condition: product of the roots = (3)/(5)
⇒ (-n)/(m) = (3)/(5)
Put m = 5:
⇒ (-n)/(5) = (3)/(5)
⇒ -n = 3
⇒ n = -3
Answer: m = 5, n = -3

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 4x² - 4x - 3 = 0.
mcqs.why: Sum = -b/a = -(-4)/4 = 4/4 = 1, substituting a = 4 and b = -4. Product = c/a = -3/4, substituting c = -3 and a = 4.

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0.
mcqs.why: Sum = -b/a = -(5)/2 = -5/2, substituting a = 2 and b = 5. Product = c/a = 6/2 = 3, substituting c = 6 and a = 2.

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 3x² + 2x - 5 = 0.
mcqs.why: Sum = -b/a = -(2)/3 = -2/3, substituting a = 3 and b = 2. Product = c/a = -5/3, substituting c = -5 and a = 3.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the roots of 2x² + kx + 6 = 0 equals the product of its roots.
mcqs.why: Sum = -b/a = -k/2 and product = c/a = 6/2 = 3. Setting them equal: -k/2 = 3, multiply by 2 to get -k = 6, so k = -6.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the squares of the roots of x² - 5kx + 6k² = 0 equals 13.
mcqs.why: Here α + β = 5k and αβ = 6k². Then α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ = (5k)² - 2(6k²) = 25k² - 12k² = 13k². Setting 13k² = 13 gives k² = 1, so k = ±1.

mcqs.q: Find k if the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0 differ by unity.
mcqs.why: Here α + β = 5 and αβ = k. Differ by unity means (α - β)² = 1, and (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ = 25 - 4k. Setting 25 - 4k = 1 gives 4k = 24, so k = 6.

mcqs.q: Find k if the roots of x² - 9x + k + 2 = 0 differ by three.
mcqs.why: Here α + β = 9 and αβ = k + 2. Differ by three means (α - β)² = 9, and (α - β)² = (α + β)² - 4αβ = 81 - 4(k + 2) = 73 - 4k. Setting 73 - 4k = 9 gives 4k = 64, so k = 16.

mcqs.q: If α, β are the roots of x² - 5x + k = 0 and 3α + 2β = 12, then k equals
mcqs.why: From α + β = 5, doubling gives 2α + 2β = 10. Subtract from 3α + 2β = 12 to get α = 2, then β = 5 - 2 = 3. Hence k = αβ = (2)(3) = 6.

mcqs.q: Find m and n if both the sum and product of the roots of mx² - 3x - n = 0 equal 3/5.
mcqs.why: Sum = -b/a = 3/m = 3/5 gives m = 5. Product = c/a = -n/m = 3/5; substituting m = 5 gives -n/5 = 3/5, so -n = 3 and n = -3.

mcqs.q: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the product of the roots αβ equals
mcqs.why: The two root relations are α + β = -b/a (sum) and αβ = c/a (product). For example, in 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0 the product is c/a = 6/2 = 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A symmetric function of the roots is unchanged when α and β are interchanged.
  • α³β + β³α = c(b² - 2ac)/a³ and (α - β)² = (b² - 4ac)/a² for the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0.
  • The equation with given roots is x² - (sum of roots)x + (product of roots) = 0.
  • Roots 3 + √2 and 3 - √2 give sum 6 and product 7, hence the equation x² - 6x + 7 = 0.
  • For the roots of 2x² + 3x + 1 = 0: α + β = -3/2, αβ = 1/2 and α² + β² = 5/4.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). If α, β are the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0, find the value of: α³β + β³α
