Collect the second elements: from (1, 2) take 2, from (2, 1) and (3, 1) take 1, from (4, 4) take 4, and from (5, 5) take 5. Without repetition Range f = {1, 2, 4, 5}; note 3 never occurs as a second element, so f is not onto.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Range and smallest/largest values are found first before forming classes.
  • Class boundaries are found with correction factor = gap/2; for a gap of 1 the factor is 0.5, subtracted from the lower limit and added to the upper limit.
  • Class mark (mid-point) = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2.
  • In Q1 (30 quiz marks) the class 66 - 75 has the highest frequency, 9, and the total frequency is 30.
  • In Q2 the mistakes data have smallest value 3, largest value 24 and range 21, giving 8 class intervals of size 3.
  • A histogram uses class boundaries on the horizontal axis and adjoining rectangles with no gaps, heights equal to frequencies.
  • A frequency polygon joins points plotted at class marks against frequencies, with end points (17, 0) and (47, 0) in Q4.
  • In Q5 the homework time 2 hours is the most frequent value, with frequency 9 out of 30 students.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Construct a frequency distribution of the marks of 30 students during a quiz with 100 points by taking 10 as the class-interval. Indicate the class-boundaries and class-marks. 40, 60, 65, 70, 35, 50, 56, 74, 72, 49, 85, 76, 82, 83, 68, 90, 67, 66, 58, 46, 74, 88, 76, 69, 57, 63, 66, 47, 82, 90.

Ans: Step 1: Find the smallest and the largest value in the data.
Smallest value = 35
Largest value = 90
Step 2: Take 10 as the class-interval, as given, and form the classes starting from 35.
Step 3: Tally each mark in its class and count the frequencies.
Class limits: 35 - 45, Frequency (f): 2 (marks 35, 40)
Class limits: 46 - 55, Frequency (f): 4 (marks 46, 47, 49, 50)
Class limits: 56 - 65, Frequency (f): 6 (marks 56, 57, 58, 60, 63, 65)
Class limits: 66 - 75, Frequency (f): 9 (marks 66, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 72, 74, 74)
Class limits: 76 - 85, Frequency (f): 6 (marks 76, 76, 82, 82, 83, 85)
Class limits: 86 - 90, Frequency (f): 3 (marks 88, 90, 90)
Total frequency: Σf = 2 + 4 + 6 + 9 + 6 + 3 = 30, which equals the number of students.
Step 4: Find the class-boundaries. The gap between the upper limit of one class and the lower limit of the next class is 46 - 45 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5. Subtract 0.5 from each lower limit and add 0.5 to each upper limit.
Class 35 - 45: Class-boundaries 34.5 - 45.5
Class 46 - 55: Class-boundaries 45.5 - 55.5
Class 56 - 65: Class-boundaries 55.5 - 65.5
Class 66 - 75: Class-boundaries 65.5 - 75.5
Class 76 - 85: Class-boundaries 75.5 - 85.5
Class 86 - 90: Class-boundaries 85.5 - 90.5
Step 5: Find the class-marks. Class mark (mid-point) = (Lower limit + Upper limit)/(2).
Class 35 - 45: Class mark = (35 + 45)/(2) = 40
Class 46 - 55: Class mark = (46 + 55)/(2) = 50.5
Class 56 - 65: Class mark = (56 + 65)/(2) = 60.5
Class 66 - 75: Class mark = (66 + 75)/(2) = 70.5
Class 76 - 85: Class mark = (76 + 85)/(2) = 80.5
Class 86 - 90: Class mark = (86 + 90)/(2) = 88
Answer: The frequency distribution is: 35 - 45 (f = 2, boundaries 34.5 - 45.5, mark 40); 46 - 55 (f = 4, boundaries 45.5 - 55.5, mark 50.5); 56 - 65 (f = 6, boundaries 55.5 - 65.5, mark 60.5); 66 - 75 (f = 9, boundaries 65.5 - 75.5, mark 70.5); 76 - 85 (f = 6, boundaries 75.5 - 85.5, mark 80.5); 86 - 90 (f = 3, boundaries 85.5 - 90.5, mark 88).

Q: Q2. Following are the mistakes made by a group of students of class 10th in a test of essay writing. Using an appropriate size of class interval, make a frequency distribution and also indicate the number of class intervals. 4, 7, 12, 9, 21, 16, 3, 19, 17, 24, 14, 15, 8, 13, 11, 16, 15, 6, 5, 8, 11, 20, 18, 22, 6.

Ans: Step 1: Find the smallest and the largest value in the data.
Smallest value = 3
Largest value = 24
Range = Largest value - Smallest value = 24 - 3 = 21
Step 2: Choose a suitable class size. Taking class size 3 gives classes covering the whole range.
Step 3: Tally each value in its class and count the frequencies.
Class interval: 1 - 3, Frequency (f): 1 (value 3)
Class interval: 4 - 6, Frequency (f): 4 (values 4, 5, 6, 6)
Class interval: 7 - 9, Frequency (f): 4 (values 7, 8, 8, 9)
Class interval: 10 - 12, Frequency (f): 3 (values 11, 11, 12)
Class interval: 13 - 15, Frequency (f): 4 (values 13, 14, 15, 15)
Class interval: 16 - 18, Frequency (f): 4 (values 16, 16, 17, 18)
Class interval: 19 - 21, Frequency (f): 3 (values 19, 20, 21)
Class interval: 22 - 24, Frequency (f): 2 (values 22, 24)
Total frequency: Σf = 1 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 25, which equals the number of values in the data.
Step 4: Find the class-boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 4 - 3 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Class 1 - 3: Class-boundaries 0.5 - 3.5
Class 4 - 6: Class-boundaries 3.5 - 6.5
Class 7 - 9: Class-boundaries 6.5 - 9.5
Class 10 - 12: Class-boundaries 9.5 - 12.5
Class 13 - 15: Class-boundaries 12.5 - 15.5
Class 16 - 18: Class-boundaries 15.5 - 18.5
Class 19 - 21: Class-boundaries 18.5 - 21.5
Class 22 - 24: Class-boundaries 21.5 - 24.5
Answer: The frequency distribution is: 1 - 3 (f = 1); 4 - 6 (f = 4); 7 - 9 (f = 4); 10 - 12 (f = 3); 13 - 15 (f = 4); 16 - 18 (f = 4); 19 - 21 (f = 3); 22 - 24 (f = 2). The number of class intervals is 8.

Q: Q3. Draw a Histogram for the following data. Class-Limit: 20 - 24, 25 - 29, 30 - 34, 35 - 39, 40 - 44, 45 - 49, 50 - 54; Frequency: 1, 3, 4, 5, 4, 2, 1.

Ans: Step 1: Make the classes continuous by finding the class-boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 25 - 24 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5. Subtract 0.5 from each lower limit and add 0.5 to each upper limit.
Class limits: 20 - 24, Frequency (f): 1, Class-boundaries: 19.5 - 24.5
Class limits: 25 - 29, Frequency (f): 3, Class-boundaries: 24.5 - 29.5
Class limits: 30 - 34, Frequency (f): 4, Class-boundaries: 29.5 - 34.5
Class limits: 35 - 39, Frequency (f): 5, Class-boundaries: 34.5 - 39.5
Class limits: 40 - 44, Frequency (f): 4, Class-boundaries: 39.5 - 44.5
Class limits: 45 - 49, Frequency (f): 2, Class-boundaries: 44.5 - 49.5
Class limits: 50 - 54, Frequency (f): 1, Class-boundaries: 49.5 - 54.5
Total frequency: Σf = 1 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 20
Graph: Histogram. Draw the horizontal axis (x-axis) for the class-boundaries from 19.5 to 54.5 with a scale of 5 units per class width, and the vertical axis (y-axis) for the frequency from 0 to 5 with a scale of 1 unit per step. Draw adjoining rectangles (bars) with no gap between them on each class-boundary interval, with heights equal to the frequencies: bar on 19.5 - 24.5 has height 1; bar on 24.5 - 29.5 has height 3; bar on 29.5 - 34.5 has height 4; bar on 34.5 - 39.5 has height 5; bar on 39.5 - 44.5 has height 4; bar on 44.5 - 49.5 has height 2; bar on 49.5 - 54.5 has height 1.
Answer: The histogram consists of the 7 adjoining bars described above, the tallest bar (height 5) standing on the class-boundaries 34.5 - 39.5.

Q: Q4(i). The following data give the weights in (kg) of the students in the 10th class. 25, 30, 32, 29, 24, 40, 36, 37, 28, 27, 41, 42, 35, 39, 31, 32, 34, 42, 40, 43, 36, 26, 22, 23, 42, 39, 35, 41, 39, 29. (i) Prepare a frequency distribution using a suitable class interval.

Ans: Step 1: Find the smallest and the largest value in the data.
Smallest value = 22 kg
Largest value = 43 kg
Range = 43 - 22 = 21
Step 2: Take a suitable class interval of 5, starting from 20.
Step 3: Tally each weight in its class and count the frequencies.
Class limits: 20 - 24, Frequency (f): 3 (weights 22, 23, 24)
Class limits: 25 - 29, Frequency (f): 6 (weights 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 29)
Class limits: 30 - 34, Frequency (f): 5 (weights 30, 31, 32, 32, 34)
Class limits: 35 - 39, Frequency (f): 8 (weights 35, 35, 36, 36, 37, 39, 39, 39)
Class limits: 40 - 44, Frequency (f): 8 (weights 40, 40, 41, 41, 42, 42, 42, 43)
Total frequency: Σf = 3 + 6 + 5 + 8 + 8 = 30, which equals the number of students.
Answer: The frequency distribution is: 20 - 24 (f = 3); 25 - 29 (f = 6); 30 - 34 (f = 5); 35 - 39 (f = 8); 40 - 44 (f = 8).

Q: Q4(ii). The following data give the weights in (kg) of the students in the 10th class. 25, 30, 32, 29, 24, 40, 36, 37, 28, 27, 41, 42, 35, 39, 31, 32, 34, 42, 40, 43, 36, 26, 22, 23, 42, 39, 35, 41, 39, 29. (ii) Draw histogram and frequency polygon.

Ans: Step 1: Use the frequency distribution of part (i): Class limits: 20 - 24, 25 - 29, 30 - 34, 35 - 39, 40 - 44; Frequencies: 3, 6, 5, 8, 8.
Step 2: Find the class-boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 25 - 24 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Class 20 - 24: Class-boundaries 19.5 - 24.5, Class mark = (20 + 24)/(2) = 22, Frequency = 3
Class 25 - 29: Class-boundaries 24.5 - 29.5, Class mark = (25 + 29)/(2) = 27, Frequency = 6
Class 30 - 34: Class-boundaries 29.5 - 34.5, Class mark = (30 + 34)/(2) = 32, Frequency = 5
Class 35 - 39: Class-boundaries 34.5 - 39.5, Class mark = (35 + 39)/(2) = 37, Frequency = 8
Class 40 - 44: Class-boundaries 39.5 - 44.5, Class mark = (40 + 44)/(2) = 42, Frequency = 8
Graph: Histogram. Draw the horizontal axis for the class-boundaries from 19.5 to 44.5 with a scale of 5 units per class width, and the vertical axis for the frequency from 0 to 8 with a scale of 1 unit per step. Draw adjoining rectangles with no gap: bar on 19.5 - 24.5 has height 3; bar on 24.5 - 29.5 has height 6; bar on 29.5 - 34.5 has height 5; bar on 34.5 - 39.5 has height 8; bar on 39.5 - 44.5 has height 8.
Graph: Frequency polygon. On the same axes, plot the points at the class marks against the frequencies: (22, 3), (27, 6), (32, 5), (37, 8), (42, 8). Add the two end points on the horizontal axis at the class marks of the imaginary classes before and after: (17, 0) and (47, 0). Join all the points in order by straight line segments.
Answer: The histogram has bars of heights 3, 6, 5, 8, 8 on the successive class-boundary intervals, and the frequency polygon joins the points (17, 0), (22, 3), (27, 6), (32, 5), (37, 8), (42, 8), (47, 0).

Q: Q5. A teacher asked the students about their time spent on homework completion time. The following set of data was obtained (Time in hours). 4, 4, 6, 3, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 4, 1, 2, 5, 3, 4, 5, 2, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6, 2. Construct a frequency table and draw a histogram showing the results.

Ans: Step 1: The data are discrete. Count how many times each value occurs.
Value (x): 1, Frequency (f): 6
Value (x): 2, Frequency (f): 9
Value (x): 3, Frequency (f): 6
Value (x): 4, Frequency (f): 5
Value (x): 5, Frequency (f): 2
Value (x): 6, Frequency (f): 2
Total frequency: Σf = 6 + 9 + 6 + 5 + 2 + 2 = 30, which equals the number of students.
Step 2: Group the values in classes of size 2 for the histogram.
Class interval: 1 - 2, Frequency (f): 6 + 9 = 15, Class-boundaries: 0.5 - 2.5
Class interval: 3 - 4, Frequency (f): 6 + 5 = 11, Class-boundaries: 2.5 - 4.5
Class interval: 5 - 6, Frequency (f): 2 + 2 = 4, Class-boundaries: 4.5 - 6.5
Total frequency: Σf = 15 + 11 + 4 = 30
Graph: Histogram. Draw the horizontal axis for the class-boundaries (time in hours) from 0.5 to 6.5 with a scale of 2 units per class width, and the vertical axis for the frequency from 0 to 15 with a scale of 1 unit per step (or 5 units per larger step). Draw adjoining rectangles with no gap: bar on 0.5 - 2.5 has height 15; bar on 2.5 - 4.5 has height 11; bar on 4.5 - 6.5 has height 4.
Answer: The frequency table is: 1 hour (f = 6); 2 hours (f = 9); 3 hours (f = 6); 4 hours (f = 5); 5 hours (f = 2); 6 hours (f = 2); grouped as 1 - 2 (f = 15), 3 - 4 (f = 11), 5 - 6 (f = 4), and the histogram has bars of heights 15, 11 and 4 on the boundary intervals 0.5 - 2.5, 2.5 - 4.5 and 4.5 - 6.5 hours respectively.

mcqs.q: In Q1, which class of the quiz marks has the highest frequency, and what is that frequency?
mcqs.why: Counting the 30 marks class by class gives frequencies 2, 4, 6, 9, 6, 3. The largest count is 9, for the marks 66, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 72, 74, 74 in the class 66 - 75.

mcqs.q: What is the class mark of the class 66 - 75 in Q1?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (66 + 75) / 2 = 141 / 2 = 70.5.

mcqs.q: What are the class boundaries of the class 35 - 45 in Q1?
mcqs.why: The gap between classes is 46 - 45 = 1, so the correction factor is 1 / 2 = 0.5. Lower boundary = 35 - 0.5 = 34.5 and upper boundary = 45 + 0.5 = 45.5.

mcqs.q: In Q2, what is the range of the mistakes data?
mcqs.why: Range = largest value - smallest value. The largest number of mistakes is 24 and the smallest is 3, so range = 24 - 3 = 21.

mcqs.q: In Q2, how many class intervals of size 3 are formed?
mcqs.why: The classes are 1 - 3, 4 - 6, 7 - 9, 10 - 12, 13 - 15, 16 - 18, 19 - 21 and 22 - 24. Counting them one by one gives 8 class intervals covering all 25 values.

mcqs.q: In Q3, on which class boundaries does the tallest histogram bar stand, and what is its height?
mcqs.why: The frequencies are 1, 3, 4, 5, 4, 2, 1, so the greatest frequency is 5. It belongs to the class 35 - 39, whose boundaries are 35 - 0.5 = 34.5 and 39 + 0.5 = 39.5.

mcqs.q: In Q4, which classes of student weights have the joint highest frequency of 8?
mcqs.why: Tallies give frequencies 3, 6, 5, 8, 8 for the classes 20 - 24 up to 40 - 44. The value 8 occurs twice, for 35 - 39 (35, 35, 36, 36, 37, 39, 39, 39) and 40 - 44 (40, 40, 41, 41, 42, 42, 42, 43).

mcqs.q: In Q4, what is the class mark of the weight class 40 - 44?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (40 + 44) / 2 = 84 / 2 = 42, the point used for the frequency polygon at frequency 8.

mcqs.q: In Q5, which homework time is most frequent, and how many students reported it?
mcqs.why: Counting the 30 times: 1 hour occurs 6 times, 2 hours 9 times, 3 hours 6 times, 4 hours 5 times, 5 hours 2 times and 6 hours 2 times. The largest count is 9, for 2 hours.

mcqs.q: In Q5, what is the frequency of the grouped class 1 - 2 hours?
mcqs.why: Grouped frequency = frequency of 1 hour + frequency of 2 hours = 6 + 9 = 15. Its class boundaries are 0.5 - 2.5, so the histogram bar there has height 15.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Less-than cumulative frequency is found by adding frequencies successively from the first class onwards.
  • A cumulative frequency polygon (ogive) is plotted at the upper class boundaries against the cumulative frequencies.
  • In Q1 the wages distribution (20 workers) ends with cumulative frequency 20 at the class 145 - 154.
  • In Q2 the ages table has 100 persons in total and the last cumulative frequency equals 100.
  • In Q4 the total number of students is 21; the less-than ogive rises while the more-than ogive falls.
  • From Q4's data: 20 students scored more than 50 marks, 6 scored less than 70 marks and 5 scored between 50 and 70.
  • The class interval of the Q4 classes is 10, and the lower class boundary of the 5th class (80 - 89) is 79.5.
  • In Q6 the salary ogive reaches cumulative frequency 20 at the upper boundary 7000.5 and 40 at 11000.5.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). The following data give the wages (in Rs) of workers. 60, 75, 80, 85, 90, 84, 70, 73, 76, 84, 95, 100, 150, 66, 58, 90, 98, 120, 77, 90. By taking 10 as the class-interval, prepare (i) Cumulative frequency distribution.

Ans: Step 1: Find the smallest and the largest value in the data.
Smallest value = 58
Largest value = 150
Step 2: Taking 10 as the class-interval, form the classes starting from 55 and tally the wages.
Class limits: 55 - 64, Frequency (f): 2 (wages 58, 60)
Class limits: 65 - 74, Frequency (f): 3 (wages 66, 70, 73)
Class limits: 75 - 84, Frequency (f): 6 (wages 75, 76, 77, 80, 84, 84)
Class limits: 85 - 94, Frequency (f): 4 (wages 85, 90, 90, 90)
Class limits: 95 - 104, Frequency (f): 3 (wages 95, 98, 100)
Class limits: 105 - 114, Frequency (f): 0
Class limits: 115 - 124, Frequency (f): 1 (wage 120)
Class limits: 125 - 134, Frequency (f): 0
Class limits: 135 - 144, Frequency (f): 0
Class limits: 145 - 154, Frequency (f): 1 (wage 150)
Total frequency: Σf = 2 + 3 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 20, which equals the number of workers.
Step 3: Add the frequencies successively to get the (less than) cumulative frequencies.
Class 55 - 64: c.f. = 2
Class 65 - 74: c.f. = 2 + 3 = 5
Class 75 - 84: c.f. = 5 + 6 = 11
Class 85 - 94: c.f. = 11 + 4 = 15
Class 95 - 104: c.f. = 15 + 3 = 18
Class 105 - 114: c.f. = 18 + 0 = 18
Class 115 - 124: c.f. = 18 + 1 = 19
Class 125 - 134: c.f. = 19 + 0 = 19
Class 135 - 144: c.f. = 19 + 0 = 19
Class 145 - 154: c.f. = 19 + 1 = 20
Answer: The cumulative frequency distribution is: 55 - 64 (c.f. 2); 65 - 74 (c.f. 5); 75 - 84 (c.f. 11); 85 - 94 (c.f. 15); 95 - 104 (c.f. 18); 105 - 114 (c.f. 18); 115 - 124 (c.f. 19); 125 - 134 (c.f. 19); 135 - 144 (c.f. 19); 145 - 154 (c.f. 20).

Q: Q1(ii). The following data give the wages (in Rs) of workers. 60, 75, 80, 85, 90, 84, 70, 73, 76, 84, 95, 100, 150, 66, 58, 90, 98, 120, 77, 90. By taking 10 as the class-interval, prepare (ii) Cumulative frequency polygon.

Ans: Step 1: Use the cumulative frequency distribution of part (i). Find the upper class boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 65 - 64 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5, and each upper boundary is the upper limit + 0.5.
Class 55 - 64: Upper class boundary 64.5, Cumulative frequency 2
Class 65 - 74: Upper class boundary 74.5, Cumulative frequency 5
Class 75 - 84: Upper class boundary 84.5, Cumulative frequency 11
Class 85 - 94: Upper class boundary 94.5, Cumulative frequency 15
Class 95 - 104: Upper class boundary 104.5, Cumulative frequency 18
Class 105 - 114: Upper class boundary 114.5, Cumulative frequency 18
Class 115 - 124: Upper class boundary 124.5, Cumulative frequency 19
Class 125 - 134: Upper class boundary 134.5, Cumulative frequency 19
Class 135 - 144: Upper class boundary 144.5, Cumulative frequency 19
Class 145 - 154: Upper class boundary 154.5, Cumulative frequency 20
Graph: Cumulative frequency polygon (ogive). Draw the horizontal axis for the upper class boundaries from 64.5 to 154.5 with a scale of 10 units per step, and the vertical axis for the cumulative frequency from 0 to 20 with a scale of 2 units per step. Plot the points (64.5, 2), (74.5, 5), (84.5, 11), (94.5, 15), (104.5, 18), (114.5, 18), (124.5, 19), (134.5, 19), (144.5, 19), (154.5, 20) and join them in order by straight line segments (or a freehand curve), starting from (54.5, 0) on the horizontal axis.
Answer: The cumulative frequency polygon (ogive) passes through the points (64.5, 2), (74.5, 5), (84.5, 11), (94.5, 15), (104.5, 18), (114.5, 18), (124.5, 19), (134.5, 19), (144.5, 19) and (154.5, 20).

Q: Q2. Make cumulative frequency table for the following data. Age in Years: 20 - 24, 25 - 29, 30 - 39, 40 - 44, 45 - 49, 50 - 54, 55 - 59; Number of persons (f): 1, 2, 26, 22, 20, 15, 14.

Ans: Step 1: Write the classes with their frequencies and upper class boundaries. The correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5, so each upper boundary is the upper limit + 0.5.
Step 2: Add the frequencies successively to get the cumulative frequencies.
Age 20 - 24: f = 1, Upper class boundary 24.5, c.f. = 1
Age 25 - 29: f = 2, Upper class boundary 29.5, c.f. = 1 + 2 = 3
Age 30 - 39: f = 26, Upper class boundary 39.5, c.f. = 3 + 26 = 29
Age 40 - 44: f = 22, Upper class boundary 44.5, c.f. = 29 + 22 = 51
Age 45 - 49: f = 20, Upper class boundary 49.5, c.f. = 51 + 20 = 71
Age 50 - 54: f = 15, Upper class boundary 54.5, c.f. = 71 + 15 = 86
Age 55 - 59: f = 14, Upper class boundary 59.5, c.f. = 86 + 14 = 100
Total: Σf = 1 + 2 + 26 + 22 + 20 + 15 + 14 = 100, which equals the last cumulative frequency.
Note: As printed, the third class is 30 - 39 with frequency 26. In the book's Answers section this class is split into two classes, 30 - 34 with frequency 16 and 35 - 39 with frequency 10 (16 + 10 = 26), giving cumulative frequencies 1, 3, 19, 29, 51, 71, 86, 100 for the eight classes.
Answer: The cumulative frequency table is: 20 - 24 (c.f. 1); 25 - 29 (c.f. 3); 30 - 39 (c.f. 29); 40 - 44 (c.f. 51); 45 - 49 (c.f. 71); 50 - 54 (c.f. 86); 55 - 59 (c.f. 100).

Q: Q3. In a city during the first week of August rainfall recorded is as follows. Construct a cumulative frequency graph. Day: Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat; Rainfall in ml: 70, 40, 30, 35, 50, 55, 80.

Ans: Step 1: Add the daily rainfall successively to get the cumulative rainfall.
Sun: Rainfall = 70 ml, Cumulative frequency = 70
Mon: Rainfall = 40 ml, Cumulative frequency = 70 + 40 = 110
Tue: Rainfall = 30 ml, Cumulative frequency = 110 + 30 = 140
Wed: Rainfall = 35 ml, Cumulative frequency = 140 + 35 = 175
Thu: Rainfall = 50 ml, Cumulative frequency = 175 + 50 = 225
Fri: Rainfall = 55 ml, Cumulative frequency = 225 + 55 = 280
Sat: Rainfall = 80 ml, Cumulative frequency = 280 + 80 = 360
Total rainfall for the week = 360 ml, which equals the last cumulative value.
Graph: Cumulative frequency graph. Draw the horizontal axis for the days of the week (Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat) equally spaced, and the vertical axis for the rainfall in ml from 0 to 360 with a scale of 50 ml per step (bars for the daily rainfall may also be drawn with heights 70, 40, 30, 35, 50, 55, 80). Plot the cumulative points (Sun, 70), (Mon, 110), (Tue, 140), (Wed, 175), (Thu, 225), (Fri, 280), (Sat, 360) and join them in order by straight line segments to form the cumulative frequency polygon.
Answer: The cumulative frequencies are Sun 70 ml, Mon 110 ml, Tue 140 ml, Wed 175 ml, Thu 225 ml, Fri 280 ml, Sat 360 ml, and the cumulative frequency graph joins these seven points in order.

Q: Q4. Draw less than and more than cumulative frequency polygon for the data given. Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Ans: Step 1: Find the class-boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 50 - 49 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Step 2: Form the less than cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries.
Marks 40 - 49: f = 1, Upper boundary 49.5, Less than c.f. = 1
Marks 50 - 59: f = 2, Upper boundary 59.5, Less than c.f. = 1 + 2 = 3
Marks 60 - 69: f = 3, Upper boundary 69.5, Less than c.f. = 3 + 3 = 6
Marks 70 - 79: f = 4, Upper boundary 79.5, Less than c.f. = 6 + 4 = 10
Marks 80 - 89: f = 5, Upper boundary 89.5, Less than c.f. = 10 + 5 = 15
Marks 90 - 99: f = 6, Upper boundary 99.5, Less than c.f. = 15 + 6 = 21
Step 3: Form the more than cumulative frequencies at the lower class boundaries (total frequency Σf = 21).
Marks 40 - 49: Lower boundary 39.5, More than c.f. = 21
Marks 50 - 59: Lower boundary 49.5, More than c.f. = 21 - 1 = 20
Marks 60 - 69: Lower boundary 59.5, More than c.f. = 20 - 2 = 18
Marks 70 - 79: Lower boundary 69.5, More than c.f. = 18 - 3 = 15
Marks 80 - 89: Lower boundary 79.5, More than c.f. = 15 - 4 = 11
Marks 90 - 99: Lower boundary 89.5, More than c.f. = 11 - 5 = 6
Graph: Less than cumulative frequency polygon (ogive). Horizontal axis: upper class boundaries 49.5 to 99.5, scale 10 units per step. Vertical axis: cumulative frequency 0 to 21, scale 5 units per step (with minor steps of 1). Plot the points (49.5, 1), (59.5, 3), (69.5, 6), (79.5, 10), (89.5, 15), (99.5, 21) and join them in order by straight line segments; the curve rises from left to right.
Graph: More than cumulative frequency polygon (ogive). On the same scales, plot the points (39.5, 21), (49.5, 20), (59.5, 18), (69.5, 15), (79.5, 11), (89.5, 6) against the lower class boundaries and join them in order by straight line segments; the curve falls from left to right.
Answer: The less than ogive passes through (49.5, 1), (59.5, 3), (69.5, 6), (79.5, 10), (89.5, 15), (99.5, 21), and the more than ogive passes through (39.5, 21), (49.5, 20), (59.5, 18), (69.5, 15), (79.5, 11), (89.5, 6).

Q: Q5(i). Determine from the data of Q4, the following. (i) Number of students who obtained more than 50 marks. (Data of Q4: Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.)

Ans: Step 1: Students who obtained more than 50 marks are those in the classes 50 - 59 and above.
Step 2: Add the frequencies of these classes.
Number of students = 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6
Number of students = 20
Check by cumulative frequency: Total students = 21; students in the class 40 - 49 (less than 50 marks) = 1; so students with more than 50 marks = 21 - 1 = 20.
Answer: 20 students obtained more than 50 marks.

Q: Q5(ii). Determine from the data of Q4, the following. (ii) Number of students who obtained less than 70 marks. (Data of Q4: Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.)

Ans: Step 1: Students who obtained less than 70 marks are those in the classes 40 - 49, 50 - 59 and 60 - 69.
Step 2: Add the frequencies of these classes.
Number of students = 1 + 2 + 3
Number of students = 6
This is also the less than cumulative frequency at the upper boundary 69.5, which is 6.
Answer: 6 students obtained less than 70 marks.

Q: Q5(iii). Determine from the data of Q4, the following. (iii) Number of students who secured marks between 50 and 70. (Data of Q4: Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.)

Ans: Step 1: Marks between 50 and 70 lie in the classes 50 - 59 and 60 - 69.
Step 2: Add the frequencies of these classes.
Number of students = 2 + 3
Number of students = 5
Answer: 5 students secured marks between 50 and 70.

Q: Q5(iv). Determine from the data of Q4, the following. (iv) Class interval of all classes. (Data of Q4: Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.)

Ans: Step 1: The class interval (class width) is the difference between the lower limits (or the upper limits) of two consecutive classes.
Step 2: Take the first two classes, 40 - 49 and 50 - 59.
Class interval = 50 - 40 = 10
Check with the class-boundaries: 59.5 - 49.5 = 10, the same for every class.
Answer: The class interval of all classes is 10.

Q: Q5(v). Determine from the data of Q4, the following. (v) Lower-class boundary of 5th class. (Data of Q4: Marks: 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 69, 70 - 79, 80 - 89, 90 - 99; Number of Students: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.)

Ans: Step 1: Count the classes in order: 1st class 40 - 49; 2nd class 50 - 59; 3rd class 60 - 69; 4th class 70 - 79; 5th class 80 - 89.
Step 2: Find the correction factor. The gap between the upper limit of the 4th class and the lower limit of the 5th class is 80 - 79 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Step 3: Subtract the correction factor from the lower limit of the 5th class.
Lower-class boundary = 80 - 0.5 = 79.5
Answer: The lower-class boundary of the 5th class is 79.5.

Q: Q6. Construct an ogive for the following table. Salary: 4000 - 5000, 5001 - 6000, 6001 - 7000, 7001 - 8000, 8001 - 9000, 9001 - 10000, 10001 - 11000; Workers: 3, 5, 12, 9, 5, 4, 2.

Ans: Step 1: Find the upper class boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 5001 - 5000 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5, and each upper boundary is the upper limit + 0.5.
Step 2: Add the frequencies successively to get the cumulative frequencies.
Salary 4000 - 5000: Workers (f) = 3, Upper class boundary 5000.5, c.f. = 3
Salary 5001 - 6000: Workers (f) = 5, Upper class boundary 6000.5, c.f. = 3 + 5 = 8
Salary 6001 - 7000: Workers (f) = 12, Upper class boundary 7000.5, c.f. = 8 + 12 = 20
Salary 7001 - 8000: Workers (f) = 9, Upper class boundary 8000.5, c.f. = 20 + 9 = 29
Salary 8001 - 9000: Workers (f) = 5, Upper class boundary 9000.5, c.f. = 29 + 5 = 34
Salary 9001 - 10000: Workers (f) = 4, Upper class boundary 10000.5, c.f. = 34 + 4 = 38
Salary 10001 - 11000: Workers (f) = 2, Upper class boundary 11000.5, c.f. = 38 + 2 = 40
Total: Σf = 3 + 5 + 12 + 9 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 40, which equals the last cumulative frequency.
Graph: Ogive (less than cumulative frequency polygon). Draw the horizontal axis for the upper class boundaries from 5000.5 to 11000.5 with a scale of 1000 units per step, and the vertical axis for the cumulative frequency from 0 to 40 with a scale of 5 units per step. Plot the points (5000.5, 3), (6000.5, 8), (7000.5, 20), (8000.5, 29), (9000.5, 34), (10000.5, 38), (11000.5, 40), starting from (4000.5, 0) on the horizontal axis, and join them in order by a freehand curve (or straight line segments).
Answer: The ogive passes through the points (5000.5, 3), (6000.5, 8), (7000.5, 20), (8000.5, 29), (9000.5, 34), (10000.5, 38) and (11000.5, 40).

mcqs.q: In Q1, what is the less-than cumulative frequency of the wages class 75 - 84?
mcqs.why: Add the frequencies successively: 55 - 64 gives 2; 65 - 74 gives 2 + 3 = 5; 75 - 84 gives 5 + 6 = 11. So the cumulative frequency at 75 - 84 is 11.

mcqs.q: In Q1, what is the upper class boundary of the wages class 85 - 94, used for the ogive?
mcqs.why: The gap between classes is 95 - 94 = 1, so the correction factor is 1 / 2 = 0.5. Upper class boundary = upper limit + 0.5 = 94 + 0.5 = 94.5, where the cumulative frequency is 15.

mcqs.q: In Q2, what is the total number of persons in the ages table?
mcqs.why: Total = sum of all frequencies = 1 + 2 + 26 + 22 + 20 + 15 + 14 = 100. This also equals the last cumulative frequency, at the class 55 - 59.

mcqs.q: In Q2, what is the cumulative frequency up to the class 45 - 49?
mcqs.why: Add successively: 1, then 1 + 2 = 3, then 3 + 26 = 29, then 29 + 22 = 51, then 51 + 20 = 71. So the cumulative frequency up to 45 - 49 is 71.

mcqs.q: In Q3, what is the cumulative rainfall by the end of Wednesday?
mcqs.why: Add day by day: Sunday 70; Monday 70 + 40 = 110; Tuesday 110 + 30 = 140; Wednesday 140 + 35 = 175. So the cumulative rainfall by Wednesday is 175 ml.

mcqs.q: In Q3, what was the total rainfall recorded in the whole week?
In Q4, what is the less-than cumulative frequency at the upper boundary 69.5?
mcqs.why: Less-than cumulative frequency at 69.5 = frequencies of 40 - 49, 50 - 59 and 60 - 69 added together = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

mcqs.q: From Q4's data (Q5(i)), how many students obtained more than 50 marks?
mcqs.why: Students above the class 40 - 49 are 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20. Check: total students 21 minus the 1 student in 40 - 49 gives 21 - 1 = 20.

mcqs.q: From Q4's data (Q5(iii)), how many students secured marks between 50 and 70?
mcqs.why: Marks between 50 and 70 lie in the classes 50 - 59 and 60 - 69. Add their frequencies: 2 + 3 = 5 students.

mcqs.q: In Q6, what is the cumulative frequency at the upper class boundary 8000.5 on the salary ogive?
mcqs.why: Add the workers successively: 3, then 3 + 5 = 8, then 8 + 12 = 20, then 20 + 9 = 29. The class 7001 - 8000 has upper boundary 8000.5, so the ogive point is (8000.5, 29).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Arithmetic mean x-bar = (sum of x) / n; for grouped data x-bar = (sum of fx) / (sum of f) using class marks.
  • Short-cut method: x-bar = a + (sum of Dx) / n, where a is the assumed mean and Dx = x - a.
  • For even n the median is the average of the (n/2)th and ((n+2)/2)th items; for odd n it is the ((n+1)/2)th item.
  • Geometric mean = antilog((sum of log x) / n); for grouped data antilog((sum of f log x) / (sum of f)).
  • Harmonic mean for grouped data = (sum of f) / (sum of f/x), and always H.M. <= G.M. <= A.M.
  • Grouped median = l + ((n/2 - c.f.) / f) x h and grouped mode = l + ((f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2)) x h.
  • In Q6 the data 58 to 73 give A.M. = 66, G.M. = 65.84, median = 67 and mode = 71.
  • In Q9 the distribution gives median 25.13, Q1 = 21.11, Q3 = 27.73 and mode 26.17, read from the ogive and histogram and checked by formula.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. The following are the weights (in kg) of students of the 10th grade. 45, 30, 25, 36, 42, 27, 31, 43, 49 and 50. Calculate mean of the weights.

Ans: Arithmetic mean: x̄ = (Σxᵢ)/(n)
Step 1: Add all the weights.
Σx = 45 + 30 + 25 + 36 + 42 + 27 + 31 + 43 + 49 + 50
Σx = 378
Step 2: Count the number of students.
n = 10
Step 3: Substitute in the formula.
x̄ = (378)/(10)
x̄ = 37.8
Answer: The mean weight is 37.8 kg.

Q: Q2. Find the mean of the weights given in Question 1 by using short-cut method. (Weights in kg: 45, 30, 25, 36, 42, 27, 31, 43, 49 and 50.)

Ans: Short-cut method: x̄ = a + (ΣDₓ)/(n), where a is the assumed (provisional) mean and Dₓ = x - a.
Step 1: Take the assumed mean a = 36.
Step 2: Find the deviation of each weight from a = 36.
x = 45: Dₓ = 45 - 36 = 9
x = 30: Dₓ = 30 - 36 = -6
x = 25: Dₓ = 25 - 36 = -11
x = 36: Dₓ = 36 - 36 = 0
x = 42: Dₓ = 42 - 36 = 6
x = 27: Dₓ = 27 - 36 = -9
x = 31: Dₓ = 31 - 36 = -5
x = 43: Dₓ = 43 - 36 = 7
x = 49: Dₓ = 49 - 36 = 13
x = 50: Dₓ = 50 - 36 = 14
Step 3: Add the deviations.
ΣDₓ = 9 - 6 - 11 + 0 + 6 - 9 - 5 + 7 + 13 + 14 = 18
Step 4: Substitute in the formula with n = 10.
x̄ = 36 + (18)/(10)
x̄ = 36 + 1.8
x̄ = 37.8
Answer: The mean weight by the short-cut method is 37.8 kg, the same as in Question 1.

Q: Q3. Using assumed mean find the mean of the following numbers. 1242, 1248, 1252, 1244, 1249.

Ans: Short-cut method: x̄ = a + (ΣDₓ)/(n), where a is the assumed mean and Dₓ = x - a.
Step 1: Take the assumed mean a = 1244.
Step 2: Find the deviation of each number from a = 1244.
x = 1242: Dₓ = 1242 - 1244 = -2
x = 1248: Dₓ = 1248 - 1244 = 4
x = 1252: Dₓ = 1252 - 1244 = 8
x = 1244: Dₓ = 1244 - 1244 = 0
x = 1249: Dₓ = 1249 - 1244 = 5
Step 3: Add the deviations.
ΣDₓ = -2 + 4 + 8 + 0 + 5 = 15
Step 4: Substitute in the formula with n = 5.
x̄ = 1244 + (15)/(5)
x̄ = 1244 + 3
x̄ = 1247
Check by the direct method: Σx = 1242 + 1248 + 1252 + 1244 + 1249 = 6235; x̄ = (6235)/(5) = 1247.
Answer: The mean is 1247.

Q: Q4. Find the mean of the following frequency distribution. Marks obtained by students of 10th class in mathematics. Score (out of 75): 0 - 15, 16 - 31, 32 - 47, 48 - 63, 64 - 75; Frequency (f): 0, 10, 40, 70, 45.

Ans: Arithmetic mean for grouped data: x̄ = (Σfᵢxᵢ)/(Σfᵢ), where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-point) of each class.
Step 1: Find the class mark of each class. Class mark = (Lower limit + Upper limit)/(2).
Step 2: Multiply each class mark by its frequency and add.
Class 0 - 15: x = (0 + 15)/(2) = 7.5, f = 0, fx = 0 × 7.5 = 0
Class 16 - 31: x = (16 + 31)/(2) = 23.5, f = 10, fx = 10 × 23.5 = 235
Class 32 - 47: x = (32 + 47)/(2) = 39.5, f = 40, fx = 40 × 39.5 = 1580
Class 48 - 63: x = (48 + 63)/(2) = 55.5, f = 70, fx = 70 × 55.5 = 3885
Class 64 - 75: x = (64 + 75)/(2) = 69.5, f = 45, fx = 45 × 69.5 = 3127.5
Step 3: Find the totals.
Σf = 0 + 10 + 40 + 70 + 45 = 165
Σfx = 0 + 235 + 1580 + 3885 + 3127.5 = 8827.5
Step 4: Substitute in the formula.
x̄ = (8827.5)/(165)
x̄ = 53.5
Answer: The mean is 53.5 marks.

Q: Q5(i). Find the median of the following data. (i) Heights of boys in inches. 64, 65, 65, 66, 66, 67.

Ans: Step 1: Arrange the heights in ascending order (they are already in ascending order).
Arranged data: 64, 65, 65, 66, 66, 67
Step 2: Count the number of values.
n = 6, which is even.
Step 3: For even n, Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of (n)/(2) th item + Size of ((n + 2)/(2)) th item].
Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of 3rd item + Size of 4th item]
The 3rd item is 65 and the 4th item is 66.
Median = (1)/(2) × (65 + 66)
Median = (1)/(2) × 131
Median = 65.5
Answer: The median height is 65.5 inches.

Q: Q5(ii). Find the median of the following data. (ii) Salaries of 9 workers of a factory: 7000, 6600, 8000, 4500, 7500, 11000, 9000, 7500.

Ans: Note: The question says 9 workers, but only 8 salaries are printed; the median is found from the 8 salaries given.
Step 1: Arrange the salaries in ascending order.
Arranged data: 4500, 6600, 7000, 7500, 7500, 8000, 9000, 11000
Step 2: Count the number of values.
n = 8, which is even.
Step 3: For even n, Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of (n)/(2) th item + Size of ((n + 2)/(2)) th item].
Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of 4th item + Size of 5th item]
The 4th item is 7500 and the 5th item is 7500.
Median = (1)/(2) × (7500 + 7500)
Median = (1)/(2) × 15000
Median = 7500
Answer: The median salary is Rs. 7500.

Q: Q6. Find the Arithmetic mean, Geometric mean, Median and Mode of the following data: 58, 59, 60, 62, 64, 64, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 71, 71, 73.

Ans: The data in ascending order are: 58, 59, 60, 62, 64, 64, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 71, 71, 73, and n = 15.
Arithmetic mean: x̄ = (Σxᵢ)/(n)
Σx = 58 + 59 + 60 + 62 + 64 + 64 + 65 + 67 + 67 + 68 + 70 + 71 + 71 + 71 + 73 = 990
x̄ = (990)/(15) = 66
Geometric mean: G.M = Anti-log((Σ log x)/(n))
log 58 = 1.7634
log 59 = 1.7709
log 60 = 1.7782
log 62 = 1.7924
log 64 = 1.8062 (for each of the two values 64)
log 65 = 1.8129
log 67 = 1.8261 (for each of the two values 67)
log 68 = 1.8325
log 70 = 1.8451
log 71 = 1.8513 (for each of the three values 71)
log 73 = 1.8633
Σ log x = 1.7634 + 1.7709 + 1.7782 + 1.7924 + 1.8062 + 1.8062 + 1.8129 + 1.8261 + 1.8261 + 1.8325 + 1.8451 + 1.8513 + 1.8513 + 1.8513 + 1.8633 = 27.2770
G.M = Anti-log((27.2770)/(15))
G.M = Anti-log(1.8185)
G.M = 65.84
Median: n = 15 is odd, so Median = Size of ((n + 1)/(2)) th item = Size of 8th item.
The 8th item in the arranged data is 67.
Median = 67
Mode: Count the frequency of each value. 58, 59, 60, 62, 65, 68, 70, 73 occur once; 64 and 67 occur twice; 71 occurs 3 times, the most.
Mode = 71
Answer: Arithmetic mean = 66, Geometric mean = 65.84, Median = 67, Mode = 71.
Note: The book's Answers section prints G.M = 64.44, which is less than the harmonic mean (65.67) of the same data and so cannot be correct, since H.M ≤ G.M ≤ A.M; the recomputed value 65.84 is given above.

Q: Q7. A set of data contains the values as 148, 145, 160, 157, 156 and 160. Show that Mode > Median > Mean.

Ans: Step 1: Find the Mean. Arithmetic mean: x̄ = (Σxᵢ)/(n)
Σx = 148 + 145 + 160 + 157 + 156 + 160 = 926
n = 6
x̄ = (926)/(6) = 154.33
Mean = 154.33
Step 2: Find the Median. Arrange the data in ascending order: 145, 148, 156, 157, 160, 160.
n = 6 is even, so Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of 3rd item + Size of 4th item].
Median = (1)/(2) × (156 + 157)
Median = (1)/(2) × 313 = 156.5
Step 3: Find the Mode. The value 160 occurs twice and every other value occurs once, so 160 is the most frequent value.
Mode = 160
Step 4: Compare the three values.
Mode = 160, Median = 156.5, Mean = 154.33
160 > 156.5 > 154.33
Answer: Mode (160) > Median (156.5) > Mean (154.33), as required.

Q: Q8(i). From the following distribution: Daily wages (in Rs): 112 - 116, 117 - 121, 122 - 126, 127 - 131, 132 - 136; No. of workers: 3, 20, 11, 4, 5. (i) Construct a frequency table.

Ans: Step 1: The given distribution is arranged as a frequency table with class-boundaries and cumulative frequencies added. The gap between consecutive classes is 117 - 116 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Step 2: Add the frequencies successively for the cumulative frequency column.
Daily wages 112 - 116: No. of workers (f) = 3, Class-boundaries 111.5 - 116.5, c.f. = 3
Daily wages 117 - 121: No. of workers (f) = 20, Class-boundaries 116.5 - 121.5, c.f. = 3 + 20 = 23
Daily wages 122 - 126: No. of workers (f) = 11, Class-boundaries 121.5 - 126.5, c.f. = 23 + 11 = 34
Daily wages 127 - 131: No. of workers (f) = 4, Class-boundaries 126.5 - 131.5, c.f. = 34 + 4 = 38
Daily wages 132 - 136: No. of workers (f) = 5, Class-boundaries 131.5 - 136.5, c.f. = 38 + 5 = 43
Total: Σf = 3 + 20 + 11 + 4 + 5 = 43 workers.
Answer: The frequency table is: 112 - 116 (f = 3, c.f. 3); 117 - 121 (f = 20, c.f. 23); 122 - 126 (f = 11, c.f. 34); 127 - 131 (f = 4, c.f. 38); 132 - 136 (f = 5, c.f. 43).

Q: Q8(ii). From the following distribution: Daily wages (in Rs): 112 - 116, 117 - 121, 122 - 126, 127 - 131, 132 - 136; No. of workers: 3, 20, 11, 4, 5. (ii) Find the class-boundaries for each group.

Ans: Step 1: Find the correction factor. The gap between the upper limit of one class and the lower limit of the next class is 117 - 116 = 1, so the correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Step 2: Subtract 0.5 from each lower limit and add 0.5 to each upper limit.
Class 112 - 116: Class-boundaries = 112 - 0.5 to 116 + 0.5 = 111.5 - 116.5
Class 117 - 121: Class-boundaries = 117 - 0.5 to 121 + 0.5 = 116.5 - 121.5
Class 122 - 126: Class-boundaries = 122 - 0.5 to 126 + 0.5 = 121.5 - 126.5
Class 127 - 131: Class-boundaries = 127 - 0.5 to 131 + 0.5 = 126.5 - 131.5
Class 132 - 136: Class-boundaries = 132 - 0.5 to 136 + 0.5 = 131.5 - 136.5
The class width from the boundaries is h = 116.5 - 111.5 = 5 for every class.
Answer: The class-boundaries are 111.5 - 116.5, 116.5 - 121.5, 121.5 - 126.5, 126.5 - 131.5 and 131.5 - 136.5.

Q: Q8(iii). From the following distribution: Daily wages (in Rs): 112 - 116, 117 - 121, 122 - 126, 127 - 131, 132 - 136; No. of workers: 3, 20, 11, 4, 5. (iii) Calculate Median, Mode, Harmonic Mean, and Geometric Mean for the table.

Ans: From parts (i) and (ii): Σf = n = 43; class-boundaries are 111.5 - 116.5, 116.5 - 121.5, 121.5 - 126.5, 126.5 - 131.5, 131.5 - 136.5; class marks (x) are 114, 119, 124, 129, 134; cumulative frequencies are 3, 23, 34, 38, 43; class width h = 5.
MEDIAN: Median = l + ((n/2 - c.f.)/f) × h
n/2 = (43)/(2) = 21.5, so the median class is the class whose cumulative frequency first exceeds 21.5, i.e. 116.5 - 121.5.
Here l = 116.5, c.f. = 3 (cumulative frequency before the median class), f = 20, h = 5.
Median = 116.5 + ((21.5 - 3)/(20)) × 5
Median = 116.5 + (18.5)/(20) × 5
Median = 116.5 + 4.625
Median = 121.125 ≈ 121.13
MODE: Mode = l + ((f₁ - f₀)/(2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)) × h
The modal class is the class with the greatest frequency, 117 - 121 (boundaries 116.5 - 121.5), with f₁ = 20; f₀ = 3 (frequency before it), f₂ = 11 (frequency after it), l = 116.5, h = 5.
Mode = 116.5 + ((20 - 3)/(2(20) - 3 - 11)) × 5
Mode = 116.5 + (17)/(26) × 5
Mode = 116.5 + 3.27
Mode = 119.77
GEOMETRIC MEAN: G.M = Anti-log((Σf log x)/(Σf)), where x is the class mark.
Class mark x = 114: f = 3, log x = 2.0569, f log x = 3 × 2.0569 = 6.1707
Class mark x = 119: f = 20, log x = 2.0755, f log x = 20 × 2.0755 = 41.5109
Class mark x = 124: f = 11, log x = 2.0934, f log x = 11 × 2.0934 = 23.0276
Class mark x = 129: f = 4, log x = 2.1106, f log x = 4 × 2.1106 = 8.4424
Class mark x = 134: f = 5, log x = 2.1271, f log x = 5 × 2.1271 = 10.6355
Σf = 43
Σf log x = 6.1707 + 41.5109 + 23.0276 + 8.4424 + 10.6355 = 89.7871
G.M = Anti-log((89.7871)/(43))
G.M = Anti-log(2.0881)
G.M = 122.48
HARMONIC MEAN: H.M = (Σf)/(Σ(f/x)), where x is the class mark.
Class mark x = 114: f = 3, (f)/(x) = (3)/(114) = 0.026316
Class mark x = 119: f = 20, (f)/(x) = (20)/(119) = 0.168067
Class mark x = 124: f = 11, (f)/(x) = (11)/(124) = 0.088710
Class mark x = 129: f = 4, (f)/(x) = (4)/(129) = 0.031008
Class mark x = 134: f = 5, (f)/(x) = (5)/(134) = 0.037313
Σ(f/x) = 0.026316 + 0.168067 + 0.088710 + 0.031008 + 0.037313 = 0.351414
H.M = (43)/(0.351414)
H.M = 122.36
Answer: Median = 121.13 (121.125), Mode = 119.77, Geometric Mean = 122.48, Harmonic Mean = 122.36.
Note: The book's Answers section prints Mode = 119.62 and H.M = 119.44; recomputation from the printed frequencies gives Mode = 119.77 and H.M = 122.36 (an H.M of 119.44 is also inconsistent with the G.M of 122.48, since H.M ≤ G.M), so the recomputed values are given. The book's Median = 121.125 and G.M = 122.49 agree with the values above.

Q: Q9. Find Median, Q1, Q3 and Mode from the following distribution graphically. Classes: 10 - 14, 15 - 19, 20 - 24, 25 - 29, 30 - 34; Frequency: 1, 3, 7, 12, 2.

Ans: Step 1: Find the class-boundaries and cumulative frequencies. The correction factor is (1)/(2) = 0.5.
Class 10 - 14: f = 1, Class-boundaries 9.5 - 14.5, c.f. = 1
Class 15 - 19: f = 3, Class-boundaries 14.5 - 19.5, c.f. = 1 + 3 = 4
Class 20 - 24: f = 7, Class-boundaries 19.5 - 24.5, c.f. = 4 + 7 = 11
Class 25 - 29: f = 12, Class-boundaries 24.5 - 29.5, c.f. = 11 + 12 = 23
Class 30 - 34: f = 2, Class-boundaries 29.5 - 34.5, c.f. = 23 + 2 = 25
Total frequency n = Σf = 25.
Step 2: Locate the required positions.
Median position = (n)/(2) th item = (25)/(2) = 12.5th item
Q1 position = (n)/(4) th item = (25)/(4) = 6.25th item
Q3 position = (3n)/(4) th item = (75)/(4) = 18.75th item
Graph: Ogive for Median and Quartiles. Draw the horizontal axis for the upper class boundaries 14.5, 19.5, 24.5, 29.5, 34.5 with a scale of 5 units per step, and the vertical axis for the cumulative frequency from 0 to 25 with a scale of 5 units per step. Plot the points (14.5, 1), (19.5, 4), (24.5, 11), (29.5, 23), (34.5, 25), starting from (9.5, 0), and join them by a curve. From the cumulative frequency 12.5 on the vertical axis draw a horizontal line to the ogive and then a vertical line down to the horizontal axis; it meets the axis at about 25.13, the median. In the same way, the horizontal lines at cumulative frequencies 6.25 and 18.75 give Q1 ≈ 21.11 and Q3 ≈ 27.73 on the horizontal axis.
Check by formula: Median = l + ((n/2 - c.f.)/f) × h = 24.5 + ((12.5 - 11)/(12)) × 5 = 24.5 + 0.625 = 25.125 ≈ 25.13.
Check by formula: Q1 = l + ((n/4 - c.f.)/f) × h = 19.5 + ((6.25 - 4)/(7)) × 5 = 19.5 + 1.61 = 21.11.
Check by formula: Q3 = l + ((3n/4 - c.f.)/f) × h = 24.5 + ((18.75 - 11)/(12)) × 5 = 24.5 + 3.23 = 27.73.
Graph: Mode from the histogram. Draw the histogram with the class-boundaries on the horizontal axis (scale 5 units per class) and frequencies 1, 3, 7, 12, 2 on the vertical axis (scale 1 unit per step). The tallest bar is on 24.5 - 29.5 (frequency 12). Join the top corners of the tallest bar diagonally to the opposite top corners of the neighbouring bars (height 7 on the left and height 2 on the right); from the intersection of the diagonals drop a perpendicular to the horizontal axis. It meets the axis at about 26.17, the mode.
Check by formula: Mode = l + ((f₁ - f₀)/(2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)) × h = 24.5 + ((12 - 7)/(24 - 7 - 2)) × 5 = 24.5 + (5)/(15) × 5 = 24.5 + 1.67 = 26.17.
Answer: Median ≈ 25.13, Q1 ≈ 21.11, Q3 ≈ 27.73, Mode ≈ 26.17.
Note: The book's Answers section prints the positions as Q1 = 4.25th item and Q3 = 12.75th item, which do not agree with Σf = 25; the correct positions are the 6.25th item for Q1 and the 18.75th item for Q3, as used above. The book's Mode = 26.166 agrees with the value found.

mcqs.q: In Q1, what is the mean of the weights 45, 30, 25, 36, 42, 27, 31, 43, 49, 50 kg?
In Q2 (short-cut method with assumed mean a = 36), what is the sum of the deviations of the weights?
In Q3, using assumed mean a = 1244, what is the mean of 1242, 1248, 1252, 1244, 1249?
mcqs.why: Deviations from 1244 are -2, 4, 8, 0, 5, whose sum is -2 + 4 + 8 + 0 + 5 = 15. Mean = a + (sum of Dx) / n = 1244 + 15 / 5 = 1244 + 3 = 1247.

mcqs.q: In Q4, what is the mean of the grouped marks distribution (sum of f = 165, sum of fx = 8827.5)?
mcqs.why: Grouped mean = (sum of fx) / (sum of f). The fx values are 0 x 7.5 = 0, 10 x 23.5 = 235, 40 x 39.5 = 1580, 70 x 55.5 = 3885 and 45 x 69.5 = 3127.5, totalling 8827.5. Mean = 8827.5 / 165 = 53.5 marks.

mcqs.q: In Q5(i), what is the median of the heights 64, 65, 65, 66, 66, 67 inches?
mcqs.why: Here n = 6 is even, so median = (1/2) x [3rd item + 4th item] = (1/2) x (65 + 66) = (1/2) x 131 = 65.5 inches.

mcqs.q: In Q5(ii), what is the median of the eight salaries 4500, 6600, 7000, 7500, 7500, 8000, 9000, 11000?

mcqs.why: Count each value: 64 and 67 occur twice each, while 71 occurs 3 times (71, 71, 71), more than any other value. The mode is the most frequent value, so mode = 71.

mcqs.q: In Q6, what is the geometric mean of the data, given sum of log x = 27.2770 and n = 15?
mcqs.why: G.M. = antilog((sum of log x) / n) = antilog(27.2770 / 15) = antilog(1.8185) = 65.84. This sits correctly between the harmonic mean and the arithmetic mean 66.

mcqs.q: In Q8(iii), what is the grouped median of the daily wages distribution (n = 43, median class 116.5 - 121.5, c.f. before it = 3, f = 20, h = 5)?
In Q9, what is the third quartile Q3 of the distribution (Q3 class 24.5 - 29.5, c.f. before it = 11, f = 12, h = 5, n = 25)?

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Range = largest value - smallest value; it is the simplest measure of dispersion.
  • Variance for ungrouped data = (sum of (x - x-bar) squared) / n, and standard deviation is its positive square root.
  • For discrete or grouped data, variance = (sum of fx squared) / (sum of f) - (mean) squared, using class marks for grouped data.
  • In Q2 the waiting times give mean 7.72, median 8.015, variance 2.9443 and standard deviation 1.72.
  • In Q3 the discrete data give range 10, variance 10.38 and standard deviation 3.22.
  • Sections A and B in Q4 have the same mean 7 but different variances, 2.4 and 6.4, so Section B is more spread out.
  • The subject with the smaller standard deviation is the more consistent one: Physics (S.D. 3.15) is more consistent than Mathematics (S.D. 9.96) in Q5.
  • In Q6 the defective bulbs distribution gives mean 5.5806, variance 2.89 and standard deviation 1.70.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Find the range for the following items: 11, 13, 15, 21, 19, 23.

Ans: Range = Largest value - Smallest value
Step 1: Find the largest value in the data.
Largest value = 23
Step 2: Find the smallest value in the data.
Smallest value = 11
Step 3: Subtract.
Range = 23 - 11
Range = 12
Answer: The range is 12.

Q: Q2(i). A bank branch manager was interested in the waiting times of customers. For this he carried out a survey. A random sample of 12 customers was selected and yielded the following data. 5.90, 9.66, 5.79, 8.02, 8.73, 8.01, 10.49, 8.35, 6.68, 5.64, 5.47, 9.91. Calculate the following: (i) Average.

Ans: Arithmetic mean (average): x̄ = (Σxᵢ)/(n)
Step 1: Add all the waiting times.
Σx = 5.90 + 9.66 + 5.79 + 8.02 + 8.73 + 8.01 + 10.49 + 8.35 + 6.68 + 5.64 + 5.47 + 9.91
Σx = 92.65
Step 2: Count the customers.
n = 12
Step 3: Substitute in the formula.
x̄ = (92.65)/(12)
x̄ = 7.7208
Answer: The average waiting time is 7.72.

Q: Q2(ii). A bank branch manager was interested in the waiting times of customers. For this he carried out a survey. A random sample of 12 customers was selected and yielded the following data. 5.90, 9.66, 5.79, 8.02, 8.73, 8.01, 10.49, 8.35, 6.68, 5.64, 5.47, 9.91. Calculate the following: (ii) Median.

Ans: Step 1: Arrange the waiting times in ascending order.
Arranged data: 5.47, 5.64, 5.79, 5.90, 6.68, 8.01, 8.02, 8.35, 8.73, 9.66, 9.91, 10.49
Step 2: Count the values.
n = 12, which is even.
Step 3: For even n, Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of (n)/(2) th item + Size of ((n + 2)/(2)) th item].
Median = (1)/(2) × [Size of 6th item + Size of 7th item]
The 6th item is 8.01 and the 7th item is 8.02.
Median = (1)/(2) × (8.01 + 8.02)
Median = (1)/(2) × 16.03
Median = 8.015
Answer: The median waiting time is 8.015.

Q: Q2(iii). A bank branch manager was interested in the waiting times of customers. For this he carried out a survey. A random sample of 12 customers was selected and yielded the following data. 5.90, 9.66, 5.79, 8.02, 8.73, 8.01, 10.49, 8.35, 6.68, 5.64, 5.47, 9.91. Calculate the following: (iii) Standard Deviation.

Ans: Standard deviation for ungrouped data: S.D = √((Σ(x - x̄)²)/(n)), and Variance: σ² = (Σ(x - x̄)²)/(n).
Step 1: From part (i), the mean is x̄ = (92.65)/(12) = 7.7208.
Step 2: Find each deviation from the mean and its square.
x = 5.90: x - x̄ = 5.90 - 7.7208 = -1.8208, (x - x̄)² = 3.3154
x = 9.66: x - x̄ = 9.66 - 7.7208 = 1.9392, (x - x̄)² = 3.7604
x = 5.79: x - x̄ = 5.79 - 7.7208 = -1.9308, (x - x̄)² = 3.7281
x = 8.02: x - x̄ = 8.02 - 7.7208 = 0.2992, (x - x̄)² = 0.0895
x = 8.73: x - x̄ = 8.73 - 7.7208 = 1.0092, (x - x̄)² = 1.0184
x = 8.01: x - x̄ = 8.01 - 7.7208 = 0.2892, (x - x̄)² = 0.0836
x = 10.49: x - x̄ = 10.49 - 7.7208 = 2.7692, (x - x̄)² = 7.6683
x = 8.35: x - x̄ = 8.35 - 7.7208 = 0.6292, (x - x̄)² = 0.3959
x = 6.68: x - x̄ = 6.68 - 7.7208 = -1.0408, (x - x̄)² = 1.0833
x = 5.64: x - x̄ = 5.64 - 7.7208 = -2.0808, (x - x̄)² = 4.3299
x = 5.47: x - x̄ = 5.47 - 7.7208 = -2.2508, (x - x̄)² = 5.0663
x = 9.91: x - x̄ = 9.91 - 7.7208 = 2.1892, (x - x̄)² = 4.7925
Step 3: Add the squared deviations.
Σ(x - x̄)² = 3.3154 + 3.7604 + 3.7281 + 0.0895 + 1.0184 + 0.0836 + 7.6683 + 0.3959 + 1.0833 + 4.3299 + 5.0663 + 4.7925 = 35.3315
Step 4: Find the variance.
Variance = (35.3315)/(12) = 2.9443
Step 5: Take the positive square root.
S.D = √(2.9443) = 1.7159 ≈ 1.72
Answer: The standard deviation of the waiting times is 1.72.
Note: The book's Answers section prints S.D = 1.71, which is the truncated value; the correctly rounded value is 1.72.

Q: Q3. Calculate the Range, Variance and Standard Deviation for the following discrete data: x: 5, 10, 11, 13, 15; f: 2, 3, 4, 1, 5.

Ans: RANGE: Range = Largest value - Smallest value = 15 - 5 = 10.
VARIANCE AND STANDARD DEVIATION: Variance: σ² = (Σfᵢxᵢ²)/(Σfᵢ) - x̄², where x̄ = (Σfᵢxᵢ)/(Σfᵢ); S.D = √(Variance).
Step 1: Build the calculation table.
x = 5: f = 2, fx = 2 × 5 = 10, x² = 25, fx² = 2 × 25 = 50
x = 10: f = 3, fx = 3 × 10 = 30, x² = 100, fx² = 3 × 100 = 300
x = 11: f = 4, fx = 4 × 11 = 44, x² = 121, fx² = 4 × 121 = 484
x = 13: f = 1, fx = 1 × 13 = 13, x² = 169, fx² = 1 × 169 = 169
x = 15: f = 5, fx = 5 × 15 = 75, x² = 225, fx² = 5 × 225 = 1125
Step 2: Find the totals.
Σf = 2 + 3 + 4 + 1 + 5 = 15
Σfx = 10 + 30 + 44 + 13 + 75 = 172
Σfx² = 50 + 300 + 484 + 169 + 1125 = 2128
Step 3: Find the mean.
x̄ = (172)/(15) = 11.4667
Step 4: Substitute in the variance formula.
Variance = (2128)/(15) - (11.4667)²
Variance = 141.8667 - 131.4844
Variance = 10.3822 ≈ 10.38
Step 5: Take the positive square root for the standard deviation.
S.D = √(10.3822) = 3.22
Answer: Range = 10, Variance = 10.38, Standard Deviation = 3.22.
Note: The book's Answers section prints Range = 65, which is incorrect for x values from 5 to 15; the correct range is 15 - 5 = 10. The book's Variance = 10.38 and S.D = 3.22 agree with the values above.

Q: Q4(a). The following table shows the marks obtained by 10 students of two sections of 10th class. Section A: 7, 9, 6, 9, 4, 7, 5, 8, 8, 7; Section B: 6, 10, 6, 4, 2, 8, 10, 6, 9, 9. Find their (a) Arithmetic Mean.

Ans: Arithmetic mean: x̄ = (Σxᵢ)/(n)
SECTION A:
Σx = 7 + 9 + 6 + 9 + 4 + 7 + 5 + 8 + 8 + 7 = 70
n = 10
x̄ = (70)/(10) = 7
SECTION B:
Σx = 6 + 10 + 6 + 4 + 2 + 8 + 10 + 6 + 9 + 9 = 70
n = 10
x̄ = (70)/(10) = 7
Answer: The arithmetic mean of Section A is 7 and the arithmetic mean of Section B is also 7.

Q: Q4(b). The following table shows the marks obtained by 10 students of two sections of 10th class. Section A: 7, 9, 6, 9, 4, 7, 5, 8, 8, 7; Section B: 6, 10, 6, 4, 2, 8, 10, 6, 9, 9. Find their (b) Variance.

Ans: Variance for ungrouped data: σ² = (Σ(x - x̄)²)/(n). From part (a), x̄ = 7 for both sections.
SECTION A: deviations from x̄ = 7 and their squares.
x = 7: x - x̄ = 0, (x - x̄)² = 0
x = 9: x - x̄ = 2, (x - x̄)² = 4
x = 6: x - x̄ = -1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 9: x - x̄ = 2, (x - x̄)² = 4
x = 4: x - x̄ = -3, (x - x̄)² = 9
x = 7: x - x̄ = 0, (x - x̄)² = 0
x = 5: x - x̄ = -2, (x - x̄)² = 4
x = 8: x - x̄ = 1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 8: x - x̄ = 1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 7: x - x̄ = 0, (x - x̄)² = 0
Σ(x - x̄)² = 0 + 4 + 1 + 4 + 9 + 0 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 24
Variance of Section A = (24)/(10) = 2.4
SECTION B: deviations from x̄ = 7 and their squares.
x = 6: x - x̄ = -1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 10: x - x̄ = 3, (x - x̄)² = 9
x = 6: x - x̄ = -1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 4: x - x̄ = -3, (x - x̄)² = 9
x = 2: x - x̄ = -5, (x - x̄)² = 25
x = 8: x - x̄ = 1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 10: x - x̄ = 3, (x - x̄)² = 9
x = 6: x - x̄ = -1, (x - x̄)² = 1
x = 9: x - x̄ = 2, (x - x̄)² = 4
x = 9: x - x̄ = 2, (x - x̄)² = 4
Σ(x - x̄)² = 1 + 9 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 1 + 9 + 1 + 4 + 4 = 64
Variance of Section B = (64)/(10) = 6.4
Answer: Variance of Section A = 2.4 and Variance of Section B = 6.4.

Q: Q5. Following are the marks (out of 75) of the eight students in two subjects. Student: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H; Marks in Mathematics: 54, 63, 59, 45, 52, 35, 61, 68; Physics: 52, 55, 57, 51, 56, 58, 50, 59. Compare the standard deviation of the marks and tell that in which subject students are more consistent.

Ans: Standard deviation for ungrouped data: S.D = √((Σ(x - x̄)²)/(n)). The subject with the smaller standard deviation is the more consistent one.
MATHEMATICS:
Step 1: Mean: Σx = 54 + 63 + 59 + 45 + 52 + 35 + 61 + 68 = 437; n = 8; x̄ = (437)/(8) = 54.625.
Step 2: Deviations from x̄ = 54.625 and their squares.
x = 54: x - x̄ = -0.625, (x - x̄)² = 0.3906
x = 63: x - x̄ = 8.375, (x - x̄)² = 70.1406
x = 59: x - x̄ = 4.375, (x - x̄)² = 19.1406
x = 45: x - x̄ = -9.625, (x - x̄)² = 92.6406
x = 52: x - x̄ = -2.625, (x - x̄)² = 6.8906
x = 35: x - x̄ = -19.625, (x - x̄)² = 385.1406
x = 61: x - x̄ = 6.375, (x - x̄)² = 40.6406
x = 68: x - x̄ = 13.375, (x - x̄)² = 178.8906
Step 3: Σ(x - x̄)² = 0.3906 + 70.1406 + 19.1406 + 92.6406 + 6.8906 + 385.1406 + 40.6406 + 178.8906 = 793.875.
Variance = (793.875)/(8) = 99.2344
S.D (Mathematics) = √(99.2344) = 9.96
PHYSICS:
Step 1: Mean: Σx = 52 + 55 + 57 + 51 + 56 + 58 + 50 + 59 = 438; n = 8; x̄ = (438)/(8) = 54.75.
Step 2: Deviations from x̄ = 54.75 and their squares.
x = 52: x - x̄ = -2.75, (x - x̄)² = 7.5625
x = 55: x - x̄ = 0.25, (x - x̄)² = 0.0625
x = 57: x - x̄ = 2.25, (x - x̄)² = 5.0625
x = 51: x - x̄ = -3.75, (x - x̄)² = 14.0625
x = 56: x - x̄ = 1.25, (x - x̄)² = 1.5625
x = 58: x - x̄ = 3.25, (x - x̄)² = 10.5625
x = 50: x - x̄ = -4.75, (x - x̄)² = 22.5625
x = 59: x - x̄ = 4.25, (x - x̄)² = 18.0625
Step 3: Σ(x - x̄)² = 7.5625 + 0.0625 + 5.0625 + 14.0625 + 1.5625 + 10.5625 + 22.5625 + 18.0625 = 79.5.
Variance = (79.5)/(8) = 9.9375
S.D (Physics) = √(9.9375) = 3.15
Step 4: Compare: S.D of Physics (3.15) is smaller than S.D of Mathematics (9.96), so the Physics marks are less scattered.
Answer: S.D of Mathematics = 9.96 and S.D of Physics = 3.15; the students are more consistent in Physics.

Q: Q6. The following is the distribution for the number of defective bulbs in 30 cartons (Packs). Find Variance and Standard Deviation of defective bulbs. No. of defective bulbs: 0 - 2, 2 - 4, 4 - 6, 6 - 8, 8 - 10; No. of packs (f): 1, 3, 15, 10, 2.

Ans: Variance: σ² = (Σfᵢxᵢ²)/(Σfᵢ) - x̄², where xᵢ is the class mark and x̄ = (Σfᵢxᵢ)/(Σfᵢ); S.D = √(Variance).
Note: The question says 30 cartons, but the printed frequencies add to 31; the calculation uses the printed frequencies, Σf = 31 (the book's Answers section also uses these frequencies).
Step 1: Find the class mark of each class. Class mark = (Lower limit + Upper limit)/(2).
Step 2: Build the calculation table.
Class 0 - 2: x = 1, f = 1, fx = 1 × 1 = 1, x² = 1, fx² = 1 × 1 = 1
Class 2 - 4: x = 3, f = 3, fx = 3 × 3 = 9, x² = 9, fx² = 3 × 9 = 27
Class 4 - 6: x = 5, f = 15, fx = 15 × 5 = 75, x² = 25, fx² = 15 × 25 = 375
Class 6 - 8: x = 7, f = 10, fx = 10 × 7 = 70, x² = 49, fx² = 10 × 49 = 490
Class 8 - 10: x = 9, f = 2, fx = 2 × 9 = 18, x² = 81, fx² = 2 × 81 = 162
Step 3: Find the totals.
Σf = 1 + 3 + 15 + 10 + 2 = 31
Σfx = 1 + 9 + 75 + 70 + 18 = 173
Σfx² = 1 + 27 + 375 + 490 + 162 = 1055
Step 4: Find the mean.
x̄ = (173)/(31) = 5.5806
Step 5: Substitute in the variance formula.
Variance = (1055)/(31) - (5.5806)²
Variance = 34.0323 - 31.1436
Variance = 2.8887 ≈ 2.89
Step 6: Take the positive square root for the standard deviation.
S.D = √(2.8887) = 1.70
Answer: Variance = 2.89 and Standard Deviation = 1.70.
Note: The book's Answers section prints Variance = 2.88, which is the truncated value; the correctly rounded value is 2.89. Its S.D = 1.7 agrees with the value above.

mcqs.q: In Q1, what is the range of the items 11, 13, 15, 21, 19, 23?
mcqs.why: Range = largest value - smallest value = 23 - 11 = 12.

mcqs.q: In Q2(i), what is the average (mean) waiting time of the 12 customers, given sum of x = 92.65?
mcqs.why: Mean = (sum of x) / n = 92.65 / 12 = 7.7208, which rounds to 7.72.

mcqs.q: In Q2(ii), what is the median waiting time of the 12 customers?
In Q2(iii), what is the standard deviation of the waiting times, given sum of (x - mean) squared = 35.3315 and n = 12?
mcqs.why: Variance = (sum of (x - x-bar) squared) / n = 35.3315 / 12 = 2.9443. Standard deviation = square root of the variance = sqrt(2.9443) = 1.7159, which rounds to 1.72.

mcqs.q: In Q3, what is the variance of the discrete data x: 5, 10, 11, 13, 15 with f: 2, 3, 4, 1, 5 (sum of f = 15, sum of fx = 172, sum of fx squared = 2128)?
mcqs.why: Mean = (sum of fx) / (sum of f) = 172 / 15 = 11.4667. Variance = (sum of fx squared) / (sum of f) - (mean) squared = 2128 / 15 - (11.4667) squared = 141.8667 - 131.4844 = 10.3822, about 10.38.

mcqs.q: In Q3, what is the standard deviation of the same discrete data, whose variance is 10.3822?
mcqs.why: Standard deviation = square root of the variance = sqrt(10.3822) = 3.22. The range of the same data is 15 - 5 = 10.

mcqs.q: In Q4, what are the variances of Section A and Section B (both have mean 7; sum of squared deviations is 24 for A and 64 for B, n = 10 each)?
mcqs.why: Variance = (sum of (x - x-bar) squared) / n. Section A: 24 / 10 = 2.4. Section B: 64 / 10 = 6.4. The means are equal (70 / 10 = 7 each) but Section B is more spread out.

mcqs.q: In Q5, what is the standard deviation of the Mathematics marks, given sum of (x - mean) squared = 793.875 and n = 8?
mcqs.why: Variance = (sum of (x - x-bar) squared) / n = 793.875 / 8 = 99.2344. Standard deviation = sqrt(99.2344) = 9.96.

mcqs.q: In Q5, in which subject are the students more consistent, Mathematics (S.D. 9.96) or Physics (S.D. 3.15)?
options: Mathematics, because its standard deviation is larger
Physics, because its standard deviation is smaller
Both equally, because their means are nearly equal
mcqs.why: Consistency is judged by spread: the smaller standard deviation means marks are closer to the mean. Physics variance = 79.5 / 8 = 9.9375, so S.D. = sqrt(9.9375) = 3.15, which is smaller than 9.96 for Mathematics, so students are more consistent in Physics.

mcqs.q: In Q6, what are the variance and standard deviation of the defective bulbs (sum of f = 31, sum of fx = 173, sum of fx squared = 1055)?
mcqs.why: Mean = (sum of fx) / (sum of f) = 173 / 31 = 5.5806. Variance = (sum of fx squared) / (sum of f) - (mean) squared = 1055 / 31 - (5.5806) squared = 34.0323 - 31.1436 = 2.8887, about 2.89. S.D. = sqrt(2.8887) = 1.70.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Class interval is the difference between the upper limits (or lower limits) of two consecutive classes; range is the difference between the largest and smallest values.
  • A cumulative frequency graph or polygon is called an ogive, while a frequency polygon joins points at class marks against frequencies.
  • Mean = (sum of x) / n, so the total of a data set = mean x n; variance = (sum of f(x - x-bar) squared) / (sum of f) and standard deviation is its square root.
  • The mode is the most frequent value; data with all values equal have standard deviation 0.
  • In Q2 the ages of 27 students group as 15 - 16 (f = 12), 17 - 18 (f = 12) and 19 - 20 (f = 3).
  • In Q4 the frequency polygon peaks at class mark 27 with frequency 25, joining points (5, 2), (16, 7), (27, 25), (38, 11), (47, 5).
  • In the Project (53 test scores) the range is 55 - 25 = 30, the grouped mean is 2165 / 53 = 40.85, the variance is 67.13 and the standard deviation is 8.19.
  • In Q5 the cumulative frequencies for the boys' weights reach 151 at the upper boundary 59.95 and 240 at 71.95.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). At the end of each question, four circles are given. Fill in the correct circle only. (i) The difference between upper limit of two consecutive classes in a frequency table is called.

Options: (a) Class limit (b) Class interval (c) Class mark (d) Range

Correct answer: Class interval

Q: Q1(ii). A cumulative frequency histogram is also called

Options: (a) Histogram (b) Pie chart (c) Ogive (d) frequency polygon

Correct answer: Ogive

Q: Q1(iii). The number of times a value appears on a set of data is called

Options: (a) frequency (b) average (c) mode (d) median

Correct answer: frequency

Q: Q1(iv). The data below represents the number of televisions that 11 students have in their homes. Find the mode of the data. 3, 2, 1, 1, 1, 5, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2.

Options: (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 3 (d) 4

Correct answer: 1

Q: Q1(v). In which data set are the mean, median, mode, and range all the same number?

Options: (a) 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 2 (b) 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1 (c) 1, 3, 3, 3, 2, 3, 1 (d) 2, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3

Correct answer: 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 2

Q: Q1(vi). The nth root of product of 'n' number of values is called.

Options: (a) arithmetic (b) geometric mean (c) harmonic (d) standard deviation

Correct answer: geometric mean

Q: Q1(vii). In a set of data 63, 65, 66, 67, 69, median is

Options: (a) 63 (b) 66 (c) 67 (d) 69

Correct answer: 66

Q: Q1(viii). In a set of data 41, 43, 47, 51, 57, 52, 59 median is

Options: (a) 51 (b) 47 (c) 47 (d) none of these

Correct answer: 51

Q: Q1(ix). In the given set of data 5, 7, 7, 5, 3, 7, 2, 8, 2 mode is

Options: (a) 9 (b) 5 (c) 2 (d) 7

Correct answer: 7

Q: Q1(x). In the given set of data 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5 the standard deviation is

Options: (a) 5 (b) 0 (c) 7 (d) none of these

Correct answer: 0

Q: Q1(xi). The average pocket money of 30 student is Rs. 20/-. The total amount in the class is

Options: (a) Rs. 20/- (b) Rs. 30/- (c) Rs. 300/- (d) Rs. 600/-

Correct answer: Rs. 600/-

Q: Q1(xii). The sum of 30 observations is 1500. Its average will be

Options: (a) 1500 (b) 150 (c) 15 (d) none of these

Correct answer: none of these

Q: Q1(xiii). The difference of the largest and smallest value in the data is called

Options: (a) Mean (b) Mode (c) Range (d) Standard deviation

Correct answer: Range

Q: Q1(xiv). The formula (Σx)/(n) determines

Options: (a) Arithmetic Mean (b) Median (c) Mode (d) G.M

Correct answer: Arithmetic Mean

Q: Q1(xv). What is the difference between the mean of Set B and the median of Set A? Set A: {2, -1, 7, -4, 11, 3}; Set B: {12, 5, -3, 4, 7, -7}.

Options: (a) -0.5 (b) 0 (c) 0.5 (d) 1

Correct answer: 0.5

Q: Q1(xvi). (Σf(x - x̄)²)/(Σf) is called ______

Options: (a) Range (b) Median (c) S.D (d) Variance

Correct answer: Variance

Q: Q1(xvii). The most frequent value in the data is called its ______

Options: (a) Mean (b) Median (c) Mode (d) G.M

Correct answer: Mode

Q: Q2. The ages (in years) of 27 students of 10th class are given. Prepare a frequency distribution of suitable class interval. 17, 17, 16, 16, 17, 16, 16, 17, 18, 18, 15, 17, 19, 18, 18, 17, 16, 15, 16, 17, 15, 19, 19, 15, 15, 16, 18.

Ans: Step 1: Find the smallest and the largest age.
Smallest age = 15 years
Largest age = 19 years
Step 2: Count each age (discrete frequency table).
Age (x): 15, Frequency (f): 5
Age (x): 16, Frequency (f): 7
Age (x): 17, Frequency (f): 7
Age (x): 18, Frequency (f): 5
Age (x): 19, Frequency (f): 3
Total: Σf = 5 + 7 + 7 + 5 + 3 = 27, which equals the number of students.
Step 3: Group the ages in classes of size 2.
Class 15 - 16: Frequency (f) = 5 + 7 = 12
Class 17 - 18: Frequency (f) = 7 + 5 = 12
Class 19 - 20: Frequency (f) = 3 + 0 = 3
Total: Σf = 12 + 12 + 3 = 27
Answer: The frequency distribution with class interval 2 is: 15 - 16 (f = 12); 17 - 18 (f = 12); 19 - 20 (f = 3); total 27 students.

Q: Q3. Prepare a histogram of the following table: Brand of car: A, B, C, D, E; Sale in 1 month: 100, 120, 110, 72, 169.

Ans: Step 1: The table gives one sale value for each brand of car.
Brand A: Sale in 1 month = 100
Brand B: Sale in 1 month = 120
Brand C: Sale in 1 month = 110
Brand D: Sale in 1 month = 72
Brand E: Sale in 1 month = 169
Graph: Histogram (bar graph). Draw the horizontal axis (x-axis) for the brands of car A, B, C, D, E equally spaced, and the vertical axis (y-axis) for the sale in 1 month from 0 to 180 with a scale of 30 units per step. Draw one vertical bar for each brand, with heights equal to the sales: bar for A has height 100; bar for B has height 120; bar for C has height 110; bar for D has height 72; bar for E has height 169.
Answer: The histogram has five bars of heights 100 (A), 120 (B), 110 (C), 72 (D) and 169 (E), the tallest bar being for brand E.

Q: Q4. Prepare a frequency polygon of the following frequency distribution. Score in test: 0 - 10, 11 - 21, 22 - 32, 33 - 43, 44 - 50; Frequency: 2, 7, 25, 11, 5.

Ans: Step 1: Find the class mark (mid-point) of each class. Class mark = (Lower limit + Upper limit)/(2).
Class 0 - 10: Class mark = (0 + 10)/(2) = 5, Frequency = 2
Class 11 - 21: Class mark = (11 + 21)/(2) = 16, Frequency = 7
Class 22 - 32: Class mark = (22 + 32)/(2) = 27, Frequency = 25
Class 33 - 43: Class mark = (33 + 43)/(2) = 38, Frequency = 11
Class 44 - 50: Class mark = (44 + 50)/(2) = 47, Frequency = 5
Total frequency: Σf = 2 + 7 + 25 + 11 + 5 = 50
Graph: Frequency polygon. Draw the horizontal axis for the class marks from 0 to 58 with a scale of 11 units per step (the gap between successive class marks), and the vertical axis for the frequency from 0 to 26 with a scale of 2 units per step. Plot the points (5, 2), (16, 7), (27, 25), (38, 11), (47, 5). Add the two end points on the horizontal axis at the class marks of the imaginary classes before and after: (-6, 0) and (58, 0). Join all the points in order by straight line segments.
Answer: The frequency polygon joins the points (-6, 0), (5, 2), (16, 7), (27, 25), (38, 11), (47, 5) and (58, 0), with its peak at the class mark 27 (frequency 25).

Q: Q5. This table summarises the weights in kilograms of 250 boys. Represent these data by means of a cumulative frequency polygon. Weight (kg): 44.0 - 47.9, 48.0 - 51.9, 52.0 - 55.9, 56.0 - 59.9, 60.0 - 63.9, 64.0 - 67.9, 68.0 - 71.9; Number of boys: 3, 17, 50, 81, 57, 23, 9.

Ans: Step 1: Find the upper class boundaries. The gap between consecutive classes is 48.0 - 47.9 = 0.1, so the correction factor is (0.1)/(2) = 0.05, and each upper boundary is the upper limit + 0.05.
Step 2: Add the numbers of boys successively to get the cumulative frequencies.
Weight 44.0 - 47.9: Number of boys (f) = 3, Upper class boundary 47.95, c.f. = 3
Weight 48.0 - 51.9: Number of boys (f) = 17, Upper class boundary 51.95, c.f. = 3 + 17 = 20
Weight 52.0 - 55.9: Number of boys (f) = 50, Upper class boundary 55.95, c.f. = 20 + 50 = 70
Weight 56.0 - 59.9: Number of boys (f) = 81, Upper class boundary 59.95, c.f. = 70 + 81 = 151
Weight 60.0 - 63.9: Number of boys (f) = 57, Upper class boundary 63.95, c.f. = 151 + 57 = 208
Weight 64.0 - 67.9: Number of boys (f) = 23, Upper class boundary 67.95, c.f. = 208 + 23 = 231
Weight 68.0 - 71.9: Number of boys (f) = 9, Upper class boundary 71.95, c.f. = 231 + 9 = 240
Note: The printed frequencies add to 240, not 250 as stated in the question; the polygon is drawn from the printed frequencies.
Graph: Cumulative frequency polygon (ogive). Draw the horizontal axis for the weight (kg) at the upper class boundaries 47.95, 51.95, 55.95, 59.95, 63.95, 67.95, 71.95 with a scale of 4 kg per step, and the vertical axis for the cumulative frequency of boys from 0 to 240 with a scale of 25 boys per step. Plot the points (47.95, 3), (51.95, 20), (55.95, 70), (59.95, 151), (63.95, 208), (67.95, 231), (71.95, 240), starting from (43.95, 0) on the horizontal axis, and join them in order by a freehand curve (or straight line segments).
Answer: The cumulative frequency polygon passes through the points (47.95, 3), (51.95, 20), (55.95, 70), (59.95, 151), (63.95, 208), (67.95, 231) and (71.95, 240).

Q: Project (a). The following scores were made on a 60-item test: 25, 30, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 49, 53, 26, 31, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 50, 53, 28, 31, 35, 37, 41, 43, 47, 51, 54, 29, 33, 36, 38, 41, 44, 48, 52, 54, 30, 33, 36, 39, 41, 44, 48, 52, 55, 30, 33, 37, 40, 42, 45, 48, 52. Group the data into class intervals of size 2, beginning with the interval 24.5 - 25.5.

Ans: Step 1: The smallest score is 25 and the largest score is 55.
Step 2: Beginning with the boundary interval 24.5 - 25.5, form successive class intervals (class-boundaries) of size 2.
The class intervals are: 24.5 - 25.5; 25.5 - 27.5; 27.5 - 29.5; 29.5 - 31.5; 31.5 - 33.5; 33.5 - 35.5; 35.5 - 37.5; 37.5 - 39.5; 39.5 - 41.5; 41.5 - 43.5; 43.5 - 45.5; 45.5 - 47.5; 47.5 - 49.5; 49.5 - 51.5; 51.5 - 53.5; 53.5 - 55.5.
Each interval of size 2 contains two whole scores: for example 25.5 - 27.5 contains the scores 26 and 27, and 53.5 - 55.5 contains the scores 54 and 55; the first interval 24.5 - 25.5 contains only the score 25.
Answer: The data are grouped into the 16 class intervals listed above, from 24.5 - 25.5 to 53.5 - 55.5.

Q: Project (b). The following scores were made on a 60-item test: 25, 30, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 49, 53, 26, 31, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 50, 53, 28, 31, 35, 37, 41, 43, 47, 51, 54, 29, 33, 36, 38, 41, 44, 48, 52, 54, 30, 33, 36, 39, 41, 44, 48, 52, 55, 30, 33, 37, 40, 42, 45, 48, 52. Set up a frequency table for the above data.

Ans: Step 1: Use the class intervals of part (a) and tally the 53 scores in them.
Class interval 24.5 - 25.5: Frequency (f) = 1 (score 25)
Class interval 25.5 - 27.5: Frequency (f) = 1 (score 26)
Class interval 27.5 - 29.5: Frequency (f) = 2 (scores 28, 29)
Class interval 29.5 - 31.5: Frequency (f) = 5 (scores 30, 30, 30, 31, 31)
Class interval 31.5 - 33.5: Frequency (f) = 3 (scores 33, 33, 33)
Class interval 33.5 - 35.5: Frequency (f) = 3 (scores 34, 34, 35)
Class interval 35.5 - 37.5: Frequency (f) = 6 (scores 36, 36, 37, 37, 37, 37)
Class interval 37.5 - 39.5: Frequency (f) = 2 (scores 38, 39)
Class interval 39.5 - 41.5: Frequency (f) = 6 (scores 40, 41, 41, 41, 41, 41)
Class interval 41.5 - 43.5: Frequency (f) = 4 (scores 42, 42, 42, 43)
Class interval 43.5 - 45.5: Frequency (f) = 3 (scores 44, 44, 45)
Class interval 45.5 - 47.5: Frequency (f) = 3 (scores 46, 46, 47)
Class interval 47.5 - 49.5: Frequency (f) = 4 (scores 48, 48, 48, 49)
Class interval 49.5 - 51.5: Frequency (f) = 2 (scores 50, 51)
Class interval 51.5 - 53.5: Frequency (f) = 5 (scores 52, 52, 52, 53, 53)
Class interval 53.5 - 55.5: Frequency (f) = 3 (scores 54, 54, 55)
Total: Σf = 1 + 1 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 3 + 6 + 2 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 2 + 5 + 3 = 53, which equals the number of scores.
Answer: The frequency table is: 24.5 - 25.5 (f = 1); 25.5 - 27.5 (f = 1); 27.5 - 29.5 (f = 2); 29.5 - 31.5 (f = 5); 31.5 - 33.5 (f = 3); 33.5 - 35.5 (f = 3); 35.5 - 37.5 (f = 6); 37.5 - 39.5 (f = 2); 39.5 - 41.5 (f = 6); 41.5 - 43.5 (f = 4); 43.5 - 45.5 (f = 3); 45.5 - 47.5 (f = 3); 47.5 - 49.5 (f = 4); 49.5 - 51.5 (f = 2); 51.5 - 53.5 (f = 5); 53.5 - 55.5 (f = 3).

Q: Project (c). The following scores were made on a 60-item test: 25, 30, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 49, 53, 26, 31, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 50, 53, 28, 31, 35, 37, 41, 43, 47, 51, 54, 29, 33, 36, 38, 41, 44, 48, 52, 54, 30, 33, 36, 39, 41, 44, 48, 52, 55, 30, 33, 37, 40, 42, 45, 48, 52. Build the histogram for the data.

Ans: Step 1: Use the frequency table of part (b): class intervals (boundaries) 24.5 - 25.5 to 53.5 - 55.5 with frequencies 1, 1, 2, 5, 3, 3, 6, 2, 6, 4, 3, 3, 4, 2, 5, 3.
Graph: Histogram. Draw the horizontal axis for the class-boundaries from 24.5 to 55.5 with a scale of 2 units per class width (the first interval has width 1), and the vertical axis for the frequency from 0 to 6 with a scale of 1 unit per step. Draw adjoining rectangles with no gap between them, one on each class interval, with heights equal to the frequencies: 24.5 - 25.5: height 1; 25.5 - 27.5: height 1; 27.5 - 29.5: height 2; 29.5 - 31.5: height 5; 31.5 - 33.5: height 3; 33.5 - 35.5: height 3; 35.5 - 37.5: height 6; 37.5 - 39.5: height 2; 39.5 - 41.5: height 6; 41.5 - 43.5: height 4; 43.5 - 45.5: height 3; 45.5 - 47.5: height 3; 47.5 - 49.5: height 4; 49.5 - 51.5: height 2; 51.5 - 53.5: height 5; 53.5 - 55.5: height 3.

Q: Project (d). The following scores were made on a 60-item test: 25, 30, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 49, 53, 26, 31, 34, 37, 41, 42, 46, 50, 53, 28, 31, 35, 37, 41, 43, 47, 51, 54, 29, 33, 36, 38, 41, 44, 48, 52, 54, 30, 33, 36, 39, 41, 44, 48, 52, 55, 30, 33, 37, 40, 42, 45, 48, 52. Draw the frequency polygon for this histogram.

Ans: Step 1: Find the class mark (mid-point) of each class interval of part (b). Class mark = (Lower boundary + Upper boundary)/(2).
Class marks: 25, 26.5, 28.5, 30.5, 32.5, 34.5, 36.5, 38.5, 40.5, 42.5, 44.5, 46.5, 48.5, 50.5, 52.5, 54.5, with frequencies 1, 1, 2, 5, 3, 3, 6, 2, 6, 4, 3, 3, 4, 2, 5, 3 respectively.

Plot the points at the top-centre of each histogram bar: (25, 1), (26.5, 1), (28.5, 2), (30.5, 5), (32.5, 3), (34.5, 3), (36.5, 6), (38.5, 2), (40.5, 6), (42.5, 4), (44.5, 3), (46.5, 3), (48.5, 4), (50.5, 2), (52.5, 5), (54.5, 3).
